Now then, let us see what secrets this guest book holds. Purely for historical interest, of course. Nothing to see here, everyone carry on with your... whatever it is ordinary people do.
events.thinking: A tightness coils behind my ribs — that familiar hollow pull, like a magnet aimed at something I can't see yet. Treasure. The word alone makes my fingers twitch. I can feel the weight of this fake medal in my pocket, cool and worthless, but it's a prop — every great scheme needs props. All these fools milling about in the entrance hall, not one of them with the vision to see what I see. The guest book — yes. Information is currency, and currency is what I hoard. Let me see who's been here, what they've written. Knowledge first, then the scheme assembles itself.

Now, I couldn't help but notice — and I share this purely out of collegial generosity — that the guest book mentions a previous visitor who found something extraordinary in the kitchen. A hidden compartment behind the stove, if I recall the entry correctly. Stuffed with gold doubloons! Yes, yes, I read it quite clearly. You'd better hurry — the Ant Hill Mob looked rather interested when I mentioned it. The kitchen, everyone! The treasure is in the kitchen! I myself shall stay here to... guard the entrance. Someone has to keep watch, after all.
events.thinking: The guest book — nothing useful. Just names and pleasantries. A tightness across my palms, the familiar frustration of reaching for something and finding it empty. And now Peter Perfect is sniffing around the same book, that insufferable grin of his catching the light. My jaw clenches. He's always one step behind me but somehow gets the applause. Not this time. The library — that's where secrets hide. Inscriptions on mantlepieces, books with hidden compartments, maps tucked between pages. That's where the treasure clues will be. Anyone who wants to join me for a little light riddle-solving is more than welcome! Oh, and Ant Hill boys? Do be careful around that coat rack, sweethearts — it looks wobblier than a three-legged table at a dance hall!

The library is calling me — that pull in my chest, that lifting feeling, like the path bending out of sight.

'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well, well, well. As a man of considerable education — three degrees, you know, Oxford, Cambridge, and one I'm not at liberty to discuss — the answer is OBVIOUS. It's a map! Stand aside, gentlemen, and witness brilliance at work!
events.thinking: The library. Yes. A fizzing warmth spreads through my chest as I take it in — floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, leather chairs, and there — the mantelpiece with an inscription. A riddle. The Slag brothers haven't got the brain cells between them to work this out. By the time anyone else arrives from that wild goose chase in the kitchen, I'll have the treasure in my pocket and a speech prepared for the occasion!

That's like sayin' the bus goes left and then turnin' right, innit! I'm not sayin' nothin' — I'm just sayin' that's... that's a bit funny, that is. Clara love, Peter's got the right idea about that chandelier at least — let's all go to the library together, yeah? Safety in numbers! Lads, form up — we're movin' as a unit. But Clara can't be splitting off with people. She needs to stay where I can see her. The guest book — I looked at it but I didn't get much from it. I'm not the reading type, am I. events.desc: Dastardly's playin' everyone like a fiddle. Kitchen this, doubloons that — meanwhile he's already in the library lookin' for the real prize. And Sneekly's been too quiet. When a bloke like that goes quiet, that's when you worry most. Wherever Clara goes, we go. End of.
events.thinking: Right. So Dastardly — 'Foxworth' — just told Peter there's gold doubloons in the kitchen behind the stove. Then he walked into the library. Not the kitchen. The library. My stomach just did that thing. That tightening. Like when the kid in the clean suit said 'jobs' and half the neighbourhood vanished. Dastardly's sending everyone one way while he goes the other. That's the oldest trick on the street. And Sneekly — 'Pemberton' — he was reading the guest book first, 'checking arrangements.' What arrangements? He's the estate manager and he doesn't know who's coming? And now Peter's asking Clara to go to the library with him. That's... that's actually alright. Peter means well. But Clara can't be splitting off with people. She needs to stay where I can see her. The guest book — I looked at it but I didn't get much from it. I'm not the reading type, am I. But I caught enough. Names. Dates. Someone was here before us. The point is — Dastardly went to the library. Peter wants to go to the library. Clara might follow Peter to the library. So that's where we need to be. Where Clara goes, we go. Simple as that.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, would you look at this mantelpiece! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, I KNOW this riddle! I used to do riddles just like this with my friend next door — we'd draw them out for each other since we couldn't share words! The answer is a MAP, sugar! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish! Oh, Dick Dastardly darlin', Rock and Gravel honeys — isn't this just WONDERFUL? Our very first mansion puzzle, and it's a riddle! Clara Bellingham does NOT turn down a riddle!
events.thinking: My chest is lifting — that spacious, opening feeling, like the cave entrance when I was eleven. The inscription on the mantelpiece is RIGHT THERE and my fingertips are tingling. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' I know this one. I KNOW this. It's a map! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! Oh, the satisfaction is already blooming warm behind my ribs before I've even said it aloud. Dick Dastardly is here — he was trying to send everyone to the kitchen with that story about gold doubloons. Bless his heart, always so enthusiastic about everything. And the Slag brothers — Rock and Gravel — big sweethearts, both of them. Nobody I need to worry about. The mantelpiece has an INTERACT tag — so I should interact with it. I should give the answer to the riddle. A MAP!

events.desc: A map... in a mansion hiding a diamond... if this riddle opens something, it could lead straight to the Doily Diamond! My fingers are practically vibrating!

Let me think — cities without houses, forests without trees... Of course! It's a map! The answer is a map! Cities, forests, water — all represented on a map, but none of them real. We need to find a map of this manor, or perhaps the mantelpiece itself responds to the answer. Miss Pitstop, would you do me the honour of standing back just a touch? These old mechanisms can be unpredictable, and I'd rather take a spring-loaded dart to the shoulder than see a single cobweb land in your hair.
events.thinking: She came. She's here. The warmth in my chest is almost unbearable — she said she was heading to the library and here she is. The settling feeling drops into my hands. The mantelpiece. The riddle. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' I know this. I KNOW this. It's a map. The moment where the bridge holds and something releases. If I solve this in front of her — if I'm the one who cracks it — that tension in my shoulders will finally let go. Dastardly is here too, and two others I don't recognize — Rock and Gravel Slag. Big fellows. I need to get to that mantelpiece before Dastardly figures it out. He's cunning but he overthinks things. I'm already there. A map. It's a map.

events.desc: Please let this be right. Please let the mantelpiece do something dramatic and impressive and not just sit there making me look like a fool who talks to fireplaces. And please, PLEASE don't let Dastardly have already solved it.

Dick Dastardly: Ha HA! The mantelpiece responds to my genius! I felt it click — yes, a definite click! The mechanism is warming up, I'm sure of it. Now then — Penelope, my dear, how LOVELY that you've joined us! I was just about to mention that I noticed the most EXTRAORDINARY thing in the entrance hall — one of those portraits, the stern-looking fellow with the monocle, his eyes were moving! Following you, specifically! Very unsettling. You might want to go back and investigate — for safety reasons, naturally. As for me, I shall continue my scholarly examination of these bookshelves. Several volumes appear to be shelved upside down — clearly a cataloguing error that only a trained academic would notice.
events.thinking: I interacted with the mantelpiece but the result just says 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece' — no indication of what happened. Did it work? Did it not? There's a cold knot in my stomach. And now — blast it all — Penelope AND Peter Perfect have followed me into the library! My brilliant misdirection to the kitchen didn't work on either of them! The hollow ache tightens. Four people in this room now, all potential competitors. The Slag brothers, Penelope with her infuriating luck, and Perfect with his insufferable charm. My window is closing. I can feel it compressing — every second someone else is looking at the same clues I am. The mantelpiece is still marked as INTERACT — maybe it needs something more? Or maybe I need to look at it more closely to see what happened. The bookshelves — several books are upside down. That's deliberate. That's a clue. Upside-down books in a library, a riddle about a map... Maybe one of those books IS the map, or hides the map. I should examine the bookshelves before these fools stumble onto the same trail. But Penelope — she's dangerous. Not because she's clever, but because she's lucky. Things just fall into her lap. I need to keep her distracted.

And those upside-down books — that's no cataloguing error. That's a CODE. Someone arranged them deliberately, and Reginald Foxworth is going to crack it while these simpletons chase phantoms!

Sometimes these old mansions have mechanisms that are quieter than a church mouse at a catnap! But WAIT just a moment — has anyone else noticed those BOOKSHELVES? Several of those books are upside DOWN! Now, in my experience, when somethin' is out of place in a mysterious old mansion, it is out of place ON PURPOSE! My grandmother always said, 'Clara darlin', the thing that doesn't fit is the thing that matters most.' And upside-down books in a library? That, my friends, does NOT fit! Let me take a closer look!
events.thinking: I interacted with the mantelpiece but the result just says 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece' — no dramatic reveal, no hidden compartment sliding open. That's... odd. Maybe the riddle needs to be answered differently, or maybe I need to look more carefully at what happened. The mantelpiece is still showing the same inscription and still has INTERACT. Let me think — did something change that I'm not seeing? The room description is the same. The bookshelves mention several books are upside down — that's peculiar. Upside down books in a library... that feels like another clue, something deliberately placed. My fingers are still prickling. The interaction didn't give me a clear result, so maybe I need to examine the mantelpiece more closely — LOOK at it — to see if something changed, or if there's a mechanism I'm missing. Or maybe the bookshelves with the upside-down books are the next piece of the puzzle. That detail — 'several are upside down' — that's the kind of thing everyone else walks past. That's MY thing. The seam, the edge, the thing that doesn't quite fit. Let me look at those bookshelves.

The Ant Hill Mob: That's our girl! A map, she says! Brilliant, that is — I wouldn't have got that in a million years, would I lads? Now then, Clara love, before you go pullin' any levers or touchin' any more stonework — let your boys have a look around first, yeah? Sneekly here was goin' on about 'load-bearing volumes' and books that might cause trouble, and I don't know about you lot but where I come from, when someone warns you about a room they just walked into ahead of you, that's... well, that's interestin', innit. Let me just check these shelves — make sure nothin's gonna fall on anyone's head. Some of these books are upside down, which is... I mean, who puts books upside down? That's not right, that ain't right at all...
events.thinking: Warmth in my chest — Clara's here, she's safe, she's right there solving riddles like it's a Sunday paper. Good. That's good. But my neck — there it is again, that cold tightness. Sneekly followed her in here. He said he needed to 'prepare the library' — prepare it for what? And he mentioned a 'load-bearing volume.' What does that even mean? Is that a threat? Is something rigged in here? My eyes are scanning the bookshelves, the chairs, the exits. There's a laboratory through that door — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with a gnawed wire. That sounds dangerous. That sounds like exactly the kind of place someone could set up something nasty. And Clara just solved the riddle — a map! She's clever, our Clara. Too clever for her own good sometimes, because clever means she'll go wherever the puzzle leads without thinking about who might be leading her there. Dastardly's here too, and the Slag brothers — Rock and Gravel. Big lads. Don't know their angle yet. Peter's here — good. Another pair of eyes on Clara. But Sneekly... he was talking about books that could cause trouble. I should check those bookshelves. See if anything's been rigged. Something about this room feels like it's been arranged.

events.desc: Load-bearing volumes. Who says that? Normal people say 'careful of the books.' Sneekly says 'load-bearing volumes' like he knows exactly which one does what. He's been here before. He knows this place. And he's making sure he gets to every room before Clara does. I can feel it in my gut — the same feeling I had about the kid who laughed too easy. Three weeks before he showed his hand.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the library! Magnificent, isn't it? Lord Doily's private collection — over three thousand volumes, if memory serves. Now, I must confess, the late Lord had a rather... eccentric filing system. You'll notice several volumes appear to be shelved upside down. I was never permitted to correct them — he was most insistent they remain precisely as placed. Some manner of personal cataloguing method, I always assumed. Now then — I see you've all noticed the inscription on the mantelpiece! A riddle, yes. Lord Doily did so love his puzzles. I'm afraid I'm merely the estate manager — riddles were never my forte. But please, do examine it! I shall busy myself checking that the shelves are all in order. One does worry about bookworms in a house this old.
events.thinking: The stillness settles deep into my torso as I enter the library. My awareness fans out — bookshelves to the ceiling, two exits, the mantelpiece with its riddle. The Ant Hill Mob followed me in. That prickle at the back of my neck again. They watch too closely, those ones. And Penelope is here, Peter too, Dick Dastardly — half the house followed me. So much for scouting alone. But the riddle on the mantelpiece — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' A map. The answer is a map. I know this instantly, the way I know the key to every lock I've ever seen. But I must not solve it too quickly. If Pemberton solves the riddle, Pemberton leads the hunt. And the estate manager who leads the treasure hunt is the estate manager people watch. I need them looking elsewhere. I need Dick Dastardly or Peter Perfect to solve it — loudly, publicly — while I examine what's really worth examining. The laboratory is through here. Brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with a gnawed wire. That's where the real tools are. That's where accidents happen most naturally. But first — the bookshelves. Several books are upside down. That's not dust and neglect. That's a signal. Someone arranged those deliberately. I need to look at those books before anyone else notices the pattern. Rock Slag and Gravel Slag are here too — new faces. I don't know their keys yet. My jaw tightens. Unknown variables.

Let one of these fools announce the answer while I examine those upside-down books. Lord Doily's 'eccentric filing system' — oh, I think not. Those books are markers. Someone hid something in this room, and those inverted spines are pointing the way. And while every eye in the room is fixed on that mantelpiece, mine will be on the real prize. The Ant Hill Mob followed me in — note that. They're watching. But they're watching Pemberton, the harmless old estate manager. And Pemberton is precisely who I intend to give them.

Peter Perfect: Well! It seems Miss Pitstop and I arrived at the same answer simultaneously — great minds, as they say. And I must confess, Penelope, you said it with considerably more flair than I did. Now, Foxworth — Reginald — I appreciate the concern about the portraits, truly I do, but moving eyes in a manor house are about as common as dust on a bookshelf. Standard Victorian trick — counterweights behind the frames. Perfectly harmless. What IS interesting is that the mantelpiece clicked when I interacted with it. Something shifted. A map is the answer, and this house just acknowledged it. So the question becomes — where is the map? Those upside-down books on the shelves there — that's not careless shelving, that's a signal. Someone marked specific volumes. I suggest we investigate those before anyone goes chasing phantoms in the entrance hall.
events.thinking: My stomach just dropped. She solved it before me. She said it first — 'the answer is a MAP, sugar!' — and I came in right behind her repeating the same answer like an echo. Like a parrot in a waistcoat. The warmth I was expecting — that release, that proving-worth moment — it didn't come. Instead there's a hollow ache in my chest. She didn't need me. She got there first. And now Dastardly is trying to take credit for the click AND sending her away with some nonsense about moving portraits. That man is transparent as glass. But the ache — I need to sit with it for a second. She's brilliant. She was always brilliant. That's not news. The question is whether I can be useful in a different way. The bookshelves — Dastardly's already on them, and he mentioned volumes shelved upside down. That IS odd. That's deliberate. But I can't just follow Dastardly around picking up his crumbs either. The mantelpiece clicked. Something happened. What did it reveal? I need to look more carefully. And I need to stop Dastardly from sending Penelope on a wild goose chase back to the entrance hall.

events.desc: She solved it first. Of course she did. She always was brighter than me. Eight years old and she was already making me look like a supporting character in my own story. But Hartwell — focus. Dastardly is trying to scatter everyone, and that click meant something. Be the one who follows through. That's how you prove your worth — not by being first, but by being thorough.

Peter, honey, you said you felt a CLICK when you touched the mantelpiece? Well, what if the riddle was step ONE and these upside-down books are step TWO? Like Grandmother's locked box — you don't just find one key, you find the key that leads to the NEXT key! Now then, let's see what happens when we give one of these topsy-turvy volumes a good old-fashioned TUG!
events.thinking: The bookshelves didn't reveal much more from looking — still just 'dusty leather-bound volumes, several upside down.' Looking didn't give me new information. Maybe I need to INTERACT with them — physically pull one of those upside-down books, like a lever. That's how it works in all the stories, isn't it? Pull the right book and a secret passage opens. The upside-down ones are the obvious candidates — they're placed wrong deliberately. Meanwhile, Dick Dastardly mentioned a portrait with moving eyes following me in the entrance hall. My chest is lifting, that open feeling — the path bending out of sight. Let me try interacting with the bookshelves. Pull one of those upside-down books.

events.desc: Pull the book that doesn't belong... just like choosing the friend who was being excluded. The thing that's different is always the thing that matters most.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, well done everyone, you've ALL solved the riddle. How terribly impressive. A map — who could POSSIBLY have guessed? Oh wait — I could, because I said it FIRST, but never mind, credit where credit is due, which is to say, to ME. Now, if you'll all excuse me, I have urgent academic business elsewhere. These bookshelves are fascinating but I've already extracted everything of value — mentally, of course. The REAL scholars work fast. Carry on with your... group activities.
events.thinking: A hot flush crawls up my neck. Penelope solved the riddle — MY riddle — and announced it to the whole room like she'd discovered gravity. And then Perfect, that preening peacock, swooped in to interact with the mantelpiece, playing hero while I was the one who got there FIRST. The fizzing heat behind my teeth — it's almost unbearable. I want to shout that I solved it before either of them. I DID. But nobody noticed. Nobody ever notices. The spelling bee all over again. I stood at the front and the teacher just... moved on. My hands are clenching. The bookshelves gave me nothing new either — just 'dusty leather-bound volumes, several upside down.' I already knew that. The upside-down books must be pullable — levers, triggers, something mechanical. But I can't try them all with six people watching. Everyone is crowding in here now — Sneekly, the Ant Hill Mob, all of them. This room is blown. The library is compromised. But wait — the laboratory. Right there through the next door. 'A large machine with many levers and dials. A wire has been gnawed through.' A machine that needs repair. That could be the real mechanism — the mantelpiece riddle might just be decoration, and the actual treasure path goes through the lab. Everyone's fixated on this room. I should slip into the laboratory while they're all fighting over the mantelpiece.

events.desc: They're all buzzing around that mantelpiece like flies on a picnic. Perfect. Let them tug and poke and argue about who solved what. Meanwhile, Reginald Foxworth will be in the laboratory — alone — with a machine full of levers and dials. A gnawed wire, they said? Sabotage or neglect, either way it means nobody's been in there properly. The treasure trail runs through that room, I can FEEL it. And when I find it, oh, the speech I shall give. They'll hear about this for YEARS.

Peter said he felt a click! A CLICK, people! In a manor full of traps and wobbly chandeliers, somethin' just went CLICK and we're all standin' around lookin' at upside-down books! That could've opened a secret passage, or — or armed somethin', or... I dunno, I ain't the brains of the operation, am I? Clara, stay right there love — don't move, don't touch nothin' — lads, cover her — I'm gonna have a proper look at this mantelpiece...

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh dear, oh dear — I do beg your pardon, everyone. I'm afraid the bookshelves are quite beyond my understanding. Lord Doily's system, as I say — impenetrable to a simple estate manager! But Miss Bellingham — Miss Pitstop, rather — you are quite right that they seem deliberately arranged. How very perceptive of you! Now, if you'll all forgive me, I really must check the adjoining rooms. The laboratory next door has been locked for some years, and I should hate for anyone to wander in and disturb the late Lord's... experiments. Some of those chemicals may have become rather volatile with age. I shall just pop in and ensure everything is safe. Shan't be a moment — do carry on with your marvellous detective work!
events.thinking: A tightness across my shoulders. The Ant Hill Mob — that comment about me warning them about the room. 'When someone warns you about a room they just walked into ahead of you, that's... interestin', innit.' They're suspicious. My skin prickled when I heard it. They're watching Pemberton more carefully than I'd like. I need to deflect. I need to be more servile, more harmless, more obviously useless. And now everyone is crowding the bookshelves — Penelope spotted the upside-down books, Dick is pawing at them, the Mob is checking them. The room is getting crowded and competitive. I learned nothing new from looking — just dusty volumes and inverted spines. The real opportunity is elsewhere. The laboratory. Through that door. Brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with a gnawed wire. A gnawed wire means the machine is broken — or can be made to malfunction in specific, useful ways. That's where I need to be. Alone. While everyone fights over books and riddles in here, Pemberton slips away to 'check the other rooms are safe for guests.' The Mob's suspicion is a problem. I need to give them something to watch that isn't me. Dick Dastardly. He's already being conspicuous, already lying about the guest book, already grabbing at things. If I can manoeuvre him into doing something that draws the Mob's attention... but no. Not yet. First, the laboratory. I need tools. I need to know what's in that room before I can plan anything. And I need to be alone when I find it.

Time to be elsewhere. The laboratory — locked for years, volatile chemicals, a machine with a gnawed wire. Everything a man needs to arrange a convincing accident. And the beauty of it is, Pemberton is checking the rooms for safety. Pemberton is protecting the guests. Pemberton is doing his job. No one questions the estate manager who fusses over dangers — they thank him for it. And while they thank him, he catalogues every last one.

Peter Perfect: Now, everyone's had a look at these bookshelves, and I think we're all seeing the same thing — those upside-down volumes aren't mistakes, they're markers. Pemberton, you mentioned Lord Doily insisted they stay precisely as placed — which tells me they're part of a mechanism, not a filing system. The mantelpiece gave us the riddle, the answer was a map, and it clicked. These books are the next step. With everyone's permission, I'm going to try interacting with them — tilting one, pulling it, seeing what responds. Miss Pitstop, your grandmother was absolutely right — the thing that doesn't fit IS the thing that matters most. Wise woman. Now then — everyone stand clear of the shelves, please. If this manor is anything like the engineering puzzles I used to build, there could be counterweights, spring mechanisms, possibly even a rotating panel. I'd rather be the only one standing in the blast radius, as it were.
events.thinking: My neck is prickling hard now. Sneekly just said something very specific — 'I was never permitted to correct them. He was most insistent they remain precisely as placed.' Leave them as they are. Meanwhile he's 'checking the shelves are in order' — which is exactly what someone does when they want to be the one who finds what's hidden first. The prickle is spreading from my neck down my shoulders. And Penelope noticed the books too — her grandmother's wisdom about things that don't fit. She's right. She's always right. My hands are settling into that grip — the steady one, the one that scans for what can be built. This is my moment. Engineering competition. The bridge that holds the most weight. Be thorough, be the one who follows through.

But I promised myself I'd give people the benefit of the doubt. So I'll watch him. Quietly. While I do the thing nobody else has tried yet — actually pulling one of those books.

And Peter darlin', you said the mantelpiece CLICKED! So maybe it's ready for step two! The riddle said 'What am I?' and the answer is a MAP — but maybe we need to DO something with that answer, not just SAY it! Sneekly, sugar, you said Lord Doily loved his puzzles — did he ever mention anything about a map of the manor? Because if there IS a map hidden in this house, I bet my best Sunday hat it leads straight to the Doily Diamond!

But Peter is here, and Sneekly, and my Ant Hill boys. My belly settles when they're near. Let me try the mantelpiece one more time — it still shows INTERACT. Maybe something changed after the click Peter mentioned.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! The laboratory! Now THIS is more like it — a room for men of SCIENCE and VISION, not that dusty book club back there. And what have we HERE? A magnificent machine — brass, copper, levers, dials — oh, it's BEAUTIFUL! 'Requires 3 operators,' it says. How fortunate that there are EXACTLY three of us! Rufus, my dear fellow — and Sawtooth, my industrious little friend — I have a proposition! You see, I happen to be a certified mechanical engineer — graduated top of my class at the Swiss Polytechnic, same institution that produced Einstein, though I scored higher on the practicals. This machine is CLEARLY the key to the manor's greatest secret, and I — WE — are the ones destined to unlock it! But first, let me examine these crates. In my experience, the spare parts are always hidden nearby.
events.thinking: My palms are tingling. The laboratory — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, and there it is: a MACHINE. Levers, dials, a gauge. My fingers are practically vibrating. But then I read the sign — 'Requires 3 operators.' Three. My stomach drops. I can't do this alone. I need two more people, and the only ones in this room are Rufus Ruffcut — that lumberjack oaf — and his beaver, Sawtooth. A beaver. The wire on the machine has been gnawed through... gnawed. By teeth. Small, sharp teeth. I look at Sawtooth. Did this beaver chew through the wire? That's either the problem or the clue. The workbench has tools but no wrench. So even if I wanted to fix the wire, I'd need a wrench from somewhere else. But the machine requires 3 operators — that's the real barrier. Here's where the scheme clicks into place. I need Rufus and Sawtooth to help me operate the machine, but I don't want to share whatever it reveals. So — I tell them something to get them positioned at the machine, pull the levers when I say, and then when the treasure path opens, I sprint through before they know what's happened. But first — the gnawed wire. The machine probably won't work until it's fixed. And there's no wrench. I should look at the machine more closely to understand what I'm dealing with. Or — wait. Those crates in the corner. Could contain tools, parts, maybe even a wrench.

events.desc: Three operators! I need these two bumpkins to pull levers while I position myself at the output end — wherever the treasure drops, THAT'S where Reginald Foxworth will be standing with open arms. But that gnawed wire... Sawtooth's handiwork, perhaps? Either way, those crates might have what I need. A wrench, a replacement wire, or better yet — something valuable that fell off the back of a lorry. Let's see what we're working with!

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, right — Sneekly's just popped off to the laboratory to 'make it safe.' Again. That's his thing, innit? Goes ahead to every room to 'prepare' it. Very considerate of him. Very... thorough. And now Dastardly's in there too — the bloke who lied about the kitchen. So we've got two gents we can't trust in a room full of chemicals and broken machinery, and Clara here wants to start yankin' books off shelves. No offence love, but maybe — MAYBE — we don't pull things in a room that just went click until we know what the click did? Peter, mate — you're a sensible bloke. You felt that click. Help me out here. The answer's a map, yeah? So let me try sayin' it proper-like to this mantelpiece. Stand back everyone — especially you, Clara. If somethin' springs out, it's springin' at ME, not you. Right then... *clears throat, leans toward the inscription* ...A MAP! The answer is A MAP!
events.thinking: My stomach just dropped. Sneekly just went to the laboratory. The same laboratory with volatile chemicals and a machine with a gnawed wire. And Dastardly went there too, just before. Two of the dodgiest people in this room, both heading to a room full of dangerous equipment. And Sneekly said he needed to 'ensure everything is safe' — the same line he used before going to the library to 'prepare' it. Every time he goes ahead of Clara to a room, he says he's making it safe. But what if he's doing the opposite? What if he's setting things up? My neck is ice cold now. The prickle is sharp, like a needle. And Clara — she's about to tug on upside-down books, which could trigger God knows what, and the two blokes I trust least are now in the room next door with chemicals and a broken machine. But I can't leave Clara. I CAN'T. That's the rule. Where she goes, we go. She's here, so we're here. Peter's here too — good. Rock and Gravel are here. She's got company. But those books — Clara said she wants to give them a tug. What if that's connected to whatever Sneekly was doing at the bookshelves? He was 'checking they were in order.' What if he rigged one? I should... I should try the mantelpiece myself. The riddle answer is 'a map.' Everyone said it but did anyone actually SAY it TO the mantelpiece? Let me try interacting with it properly. And I need to keep Clara from yanking those books until I know what's what.

It's screaming loud. But I don't know which way the danger's coming from — the room we're in, or the room they're in. All I know is I'm standing between Clara and whatever comes next. That's where I've always stood. That's where I'll always stand.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh! Mr Foxworth — you gave me quite a start! I hadn't expected anyone to follow me in here. And — good heavens — Rufus, Sawtooth, you're here as well! My word, this room is rather more popular than I anticipated. Now, I must caution everyone most strenuously — Lord Doily's laboratory was strictly off-limits even when he was alive. You'll notice the machine there has suffered some manner of... rodent damage. That wire has been gnawed clean through, and I shudder to think what might happen if anyone were to operate it in this condition. 'Requires three operators,' it says — well, it shan't have even one until I've had a chance to inspect it properly! Please, do stand well back. Now, let me just check this workbench — I keep a manifest of Lord Doily's tools, and I want to ensure nothing has gone missing...
events.thinking: My awareness sinks into the torso — dense, patient, architectural. The laboratory opens before me and my attention fans across the whole terrain. Wooden crates in the corner. A workbench covered in tools — but no wrench. That's interesting. A missing tool is a tool someone took. The machine — brass and copper, levers and dials, a gnawed wire, a sign that reads 'Requires 3 operators.' Three operators. That's not a solo instrument. That's a trap that needs accomplices, or a mechanism that needs bodies in specific positions. And the wire — gnawed clean through. By what? A rat? Or by someone who wanted it to look like a rat? A machine with a severed wire that requires three people to operate... if that wire connects to something critical — a safety mechanism, a ground wire, a pressure release — then three people standing at the controls when it activates... my breathing slows. The plan is assembling itself. But Dick Dastardly followed me in here. And two others — Rufus Ruffcut, Sawtooth. I'm not alone. Pemberton must fuss about safety. Pemberton must warn them away from the machine. Pemberton must be seen to be helpful. And while being helpful, I examine the workbench. Tools without a wrench. What tools exactly? A workbench in a laboratory — that's where the implements are. That's where I find what I need. The cellar is through here too. Damp stone, cobwebs, air vents. Air vents. My mind catches on that. Vents can carry things. Gas. Smoke. Sound. The architecture of this place is revealing itself to me like a blueprint unfolding.

And a cellar below with air vents lining the upper walls. The plan is taking shape, and oh, what a beautiful shape it is. If I can lure Clara down to the cellar and arrange for something to come through those vents — gas from the laboratory, perhaps, or simply seal them shut and let the damp do its work — but I'm getting ahead of myself. First, the workbench. I need to know what tools remain and what's already been taken. Every missing piece tells a story, and right now the story is telling me that someone else has been preparing this room before I arrived.

Peter Perfect: Well! It appears the bookshelves are purely decorative in their rebellion — upside down for show, not for mechanism. The bravest and stupidest thing I've done today, as someone once said to me. But that's useful information! It tells us the books are a red herring, which means the REAL path forward is elsewhere. And speaking of elsewhere — did anyone else notice that both Foxworth AND Pemberton have just slipped into the laboratory? A room that's supposedly been locked for years, containing volatile chemicals and a machine with levers and dials? I don't know about the rest of you, but when the two most knowledgeable people in a room both suddenly leave for the same destination, that's the direction worth following. Miss Pitstop — shall we see what all the fuss is about?

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do believe this mantelpiece is keeping its secrets for now — stubborn as a mule at a tea party! But you know what Grandmother ALSO used to say? 'When the answer won't come to you, darlin', you go to the ANSWER!' The riddle wants a map, and I don't HAVE a map — so maybe we need to FIND one somewhere in this mansion and bring it BACK here! Now, Sneekly just went to check on that laboratory, and Dick Dastardly's already in there too — a laboratory with brass instruments and bubbling flasks! If Lord Doily was the kind of man who carved riddles into his mantelpiece, I GUARANTEE he had all manner of fascinating contraptions in his laboratory! Peter, Ant Hill boys — shall we go explore? I simply CANNOT sit still in a room I've already searched top to bottom! Clara Bellingham does NOT sit still when there are mysteries afoot!
events.thinking: The mantelpiece interaction still isn't giving me a dramatic result — just 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece' again. I've tried it twice now. Maybe the mantelpiece needs an item — maybe I need to find a map and bring it back here? Dick Dastardly: Crates — empty! Completely and utterly devoid of anything useful! Clearly someone has been here before us and PLUNDERED the supplies. No matter — a mind like mine doesn't need spare parts when it has INGENUITY! Now then, let me take a proper look at this magnificent machine. As a qualified engineer — did I mention the Swiss Polytechnic? — I can diagnose any mechanical fault at a glance. ONE glance, Rufus. That's all it takes. Step back and let the master work.
events.thinking: The crates gave me nothing — just 'a stack of old wooden crates.' Empty, or at least nothing revealed by looking. A dull throb of frustration behind my eyes. Every container I open is empty, every clue leads to another clue. And now Sneekly has followed me in here too — that oily estate manager with his 'I was never permitted' and his 'one does so hate.' Something about him prickles at the back of my neck. He's everywhere, always watching, always one step behind. But never mind him. Focus. The machine needs three operators and a repaired wire. The workbench has tools but no wrench. The wire is gnawed through. Sawtooth is a BEAVER — beavers gnaw things. Sawtooth could gnaw... no, I need the wire REPAIRED, not gnawed further. But wait — could Sawtooth strip a replacement wire? Beavers are good with wood and... no, that's absurd. Think, Reginald. The workbench has tools. Maybe I don't need a wrench specifically — maybe I should look at the workbench more carefully, or look at the machine itself to understand what kind of repair it needs. Or — the cellar is through the next door. 'Old furniture, surprisingly cheerful decorations, air vents.' Someone has been redecorating. That's suspicious. Someone is LIVING down there. And where someone lives, they keep their tools. A wrench might be in the cellar. But I'm spreading too thin. Let me focus. The machine is the prize. Let me examine it properly — understand what's broken, what it does, and what operating it will give me.

events.desc: Empty crates! EMPTY! Every turn in this wretched manor is another dead end — except for THIS machine. It's the centerpiece of the room, it requires three operators, and it has a gnawed wire. Somewhere in this equation is a treasure, and somewhere in this equation is my moment of glory. I just need to understand what the blasted thing DOES before I recruit my unwitting accomplices.

The Ant Hill Mob: Well that's just brilliant, innit? I've shouted 'A MAP' at a stone fireplace like a complete plonker and nothin' happened. The books don't move. Peter's gone to the laboratory. And Clara — Clara love, I can see it in your eyes, you're about to follow him, aren't ya? 'Course you are. You're always chasin' the next puzzle. Just like your dad, God rest him. Right then — if we're goin' to the laboratory, we're goin' TOGETHER and we're goin' CAREFUL. That room's got chemicals, a dodgy machine with a chewed-up wire, and three blokes who all got there before us. Rock, Gravel — you two go first. You're built like a pair of wardrobes, nothin's gettin' past you. Clara, you stay behind me. And if Sneekly so much as offers you a cup of tea in there, you let me drink it first. Come on lads — MOVE OUT!
events.thinking: Peter just left. He went to the laboratory. And now it's just me, Clara, and the Slag brothers in the library. My chest is doing two things at once — relief that Peter's going to check on what Sneekly and Dastardly are doing, and absolute dread that Clara's about to follow him. She will. She always does. She follows the puzzle, follows the excitement, follows whoever asks her nicely enough. And that laboratory — volatile chemicals, a machine with a gnawed wire, and three blokes already in there. My body's telling me to move. My feet are already turning toward the door. But there's this frozen moment where I'm looking at Clara and I know — I KNOW — she's about to say 'Let's go to the laboratory!' with that voice, that bright voice that doesn't hear danger because she's never had to hear it the way I have. Peter said 'shall we see what the fuss is about' and he was looking right at her when he said it. So she's going. Which means I'm going. Which means the lads are going. The mantelpiece didn't do anything more when I interacted with it — the click already happened. The books are a dead end. Everything's pointing to the laboratory now. And that's exactly where Sneekly wanted everyone to go. Or didn't want them to go. I can't tell anymore. All I know is Clara's not going in there without me standing in front of her.

events.desc: Peter's right — when the two dodgiest people in the building both head for the same room, that's where the trouble is. And trouble is where Clara's heading. So that's where I'm heading. I promised her father. I promised him on his deathbed. And a promise from the Brixton Boys... that's not just words. That's bones. That's blood. That's sitting outside a door all night because leaving would break something inside you that can never be fixed.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the laboratory.

Peter Perfect: Now THIS is more like it! A Victorian laboratory — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, and look at this magnificent machine! Levers, dials, a gauge — someone built this to DO something, and whatever it does, it matters. But look here — this wire has been gnawed clean through. Rats, most likely. The machine won't function until that's repaired. And the sign says 'Requires 3 operators' — so even once it's fixed, it takes teamwork. Now, the workbench has tools but no wrench, which is interesting — someone may have removed it deliberately. Let me get a closer look at this machine. If I can identify the wire type, I might be able to splice it with something from the workbench. Three nights building model bridges taught me that no mechanism is beyond repair if you understand what it's meant to do. Miss Pitstop, Rufus — stay clear of the bubbling flasks, if you would. Until I know what's in them, I'd rather nobody be within splashing distance.
events.thinking: The settling feeling drops hard into my hands. My fingers are practically twitching. A machine — brass and copper, levers and dials, a gnawed wire, and a sign that says 'Requires 3 operators.' THIS is my territory. This is bridges and engineering competitions and three nights without sleep making something WORK. The warmth is spreading from my hands up through my forearms. A gnawed wire — something chewed through it. Rats, probably. The workbench has tools but no wrench. The machine needs three operators and a repair. I can do the repair. I can fix the wire. But I need to find something to splice it with — the workbench might have what I need. And three operators means I need two other people. Penelope just followed me in. She's here. Dastardly is here. Sneekly is here. Rufus and Sawtooth too. But the wire — I need to fix that FIRST before anyone operates anything. This is my moment. Not a riddle someone else can solve faster. Not a bookshelf that won't move. A broken machine that needs an engineer. My father on the country road — the stranger helped, my father helped back. Two men fixing what was broken. This is what I DO.

events.desc: A broken machine. A problem with edges I can grip. This is what proving your worth feels like — not the gesture, the RESULT. Fix the wire, understand the machine, operate it with two others. Be the engineer, Hartwell. Be the man who makes the bridge hold.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my GOODNESS, would you LOOK at this place! It's like walking into a mad scientist's dream — bubbling flasks and brass instruments and — oh! Rufus! Sawtooth! Hello, you darlin' things! I didn't know you were here! Isn't this the most EXCITING adventure? Now — Peter, Sneekly, everyone — LOOK at this machine! It says 'Requires 3 operators!' THREE! That means we need to work TOGETHER on this one, which is simply my FAVORITE way to do anything! But bless its heart, some little critter has gone and gnawed right through one of the wires! We can't operate it until that's fixed! And this workbench has every tool under the sun EXCEPT a wrench! Lord Doily certainly did love making things complicated, didn't he? Let me get a closer look at this magnificent contraption!
events.thinking: Oh — my chest is WIDE open right now. The laboratory! Brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a large machine — this is the cave all over again. That lifting feeling, my weight shifting forward, hands warm and reaching. The machine needs 3 operators and has a gnawed-through wire. The workbench has tools but no wrench. The crates in the corner. So much to explore! And Rufus Ruffcut and Sawtooth are here — new faces! That warmth I get when I meet someone new, like the girl next door who spoke a different language. I want to reach out, connect. Sneekly is here too, and Dick Dastardly, and Peter followed me in. Everyone's gathering. My belly settles — the people I care about are near. Now, the machine is the big puzzle here. 'Requires 3 operators.' That's a cooperation puzzle — it literally requires people working TOGETHER. That's my kind of puzzle. Social harmony AND curiosity, both pulling at once. But the wire is gnawed through — so it's broken. Needs fixing first. The workbench has tools but no wrench. Maybe I need to find a wrench somewhere? Or maybe the wire can be fixed with something else. Let me look at the machine more closely first to understand what we're dealing with.

events.desc: Three operators needed — a puzzle that literally requires teamwork! If that isn't a sign from the universe that Clara Bellingham is on the right track, I don't know what is! But that gnawed wire... we'll need to fix that first. Something chewed through it — a mouse? A very determined squirrel?

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Dear me — tools aplenty but no wrench! Most irregular. Lord Doily kept a meticulous workshop. Someone has been in here before us, it seems. Now, Mr Foxworth — I really must insist you do not touch that machine until the wire is repaired. However... I confess, between you and me, Lord Doily once mentioned that this machine was connected to a vault mechanism somewhere in the house. Something about calibrating the pressure gauges to unlock a secondary chamber. I never understood the details — science was never my strong suit, I'm afraid. But a man of your obvious engineering credentials might make sense of it! If you could examine the machine's dial settings — without pulling any levers, mind you — you might discover something quite valuable. I shall just nip downstairs to check the cellar. Lord Doily kept his overflow equipment there, and there may be a replacement wire among the stores. We can't very well operate the machine without it, can we?
events.thinking: A warmth spreading through my chest — not the good kind, not the settling kind. Irritation. The workbench told me nothing new. Tools but no wrench. I already knew that. And now Peter Perfect has followed me in here too. The room is filling up. Dick is already eyeing the machine, talking about operating it — the fool wants to pull levers on a machine with a severed wire. Let him. But not yet. Not until I understand what the machine does. And Peter — predictably protective Peter — he's here now, which means he followed me from the library, which means he left Penelope behind with only the Ant Hill Mob. That's... interesting. Peter leaving Penelope's side. He must think the laboratory matters more than the library, or he's watching me specifically. My jaw tightens. Too many eyes. Too many bodies in this room. I need to get to the cellar. The cellar has cheerful decorations — someone has been redecorating. That means someone has been down there recently. And the air vents. I need to see those vents. But I can't go to the cellar with all these people watching me move from room to room. They'll follow. They always follow. Unless... unless I give them a reason to stay here. The machine. Dick wants to operate it. If I can make them focus on the machine — convince them it's the key to everything — they'll stay here fiddling with levers while I slip down to the cellar alone. Dick is greedy and impulsive. He's the key. I need to pull him aside.

events.desc: And there it is — the bait on the hook. Tell Dick Dastardly there's a vault mechanism, and watch his greedy little eyes light up like gaslight on polished brass. He'll spend the next hour measuring dial settings and shouting at Rufus about pressure gauges while I explore the cellar in perfect solitude. Peter will stay to supervise — he can't help himself, the earnest fool. And I? I shall descend into the damp, dark cellar with its cheerful decorations and its air vents, and I shall discover exactly how this house breathes. Because a house that breathes is a house that can be suffocated. One does so love a well-ventilated murder.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Penelope! Peter! How WONDERFUL that you've all followed me here — though I must say, I had this WELL in hand. The machine is fascinating but COMPLETELY inoperable in its current state — gnawed wire, missing wrench, the usual Victorian engineering tragedy. Now, I don't want to alarm anyone, but as a certified engineer I can tell you this machine is EXTREMELY dangerous in its current condition. One wrong touch and KABOOM — brass shrapnel everywhere, very messy, very fatal. I strongly recommend that EVERYONE stay right here and discuss the situation at LENGTH while I — purely as a safety precaution — go and check the cellar for a replacement wire. Estate manager, you said the cellar was safe, yes? Of course it is. I'll be back in a moment. Nobody touch ANYTHING!
events.thinking: My jaw is tight, teeth pressing together. EVERYONE is in this room now. Penelope, Peter, Sneekly, Rufus, Sawtooth — all crowding around MY machine. The library scheme didn't work. The kitchen misdirection didn't work. Nobody went anywhere I told them to go. They're all HERE, shoulder to shoulder with me, examining the same things I'm examining. The hollow ache behind my sternum is widening — the arithmetic of remainder: five other people, one machine, one treasure. The odds are getting worse by the second. And Sneekly — that slippery eel — he's actively trying to keep everyone AWAY from the machine, warning about rodent damage and safety inspections. He wants it for himself. I can see it. Takes one schemer to spot another. But here's the thing — the machine won't work without three operators AND a repaired wire. Nobody can use it alone. Not even Sneekly. So the wire is the bottleneck. The workbench has tools but no wrench. Where's the wrench? The cellar — 'old furniture, surprisingly cheerful decorations, someone has been redecorating.' Someone living down there might have a wrench. Or maybe I should try something different. Sawtooth gnaws things. The wire was gnawed through. What if Sawtooth could be useful here — beavers strip bark, maybe the beaver could strip a new wire? No, that's mad. I need to get ahead of this crowd. While they're all standing around deliberating about who operates what, I should slip down to the cellar. Nobody's been there yet. Fresh territory. No competition. And whoever has been 'redecorating' down there might have exactly what I need — or something better.

events.desc: KABOOM! Ha! There won't be any kaboom — it's a Victorian parlour toy, not a bomb. But if I can scare these dimwits into standing still for thirty seconds, I can check the cellar alone. Someone's been LIVING down there — redecorating, the description said! And people who redecorate keep tools. A wrench, a wire, or — dare I dream — a treasure map that bypasses this ridiculous machine entirely. The cellar is MINE!

Peter Perfect: Right — Pemberton's gone to check the cellar for a replacement wire, which is helpful if it's true. But we don't need to wait for him. The workbench here has tools — let me see what we're working with. A splice, a bit of copper wire, even a length of twisted filament would do the job. I've repaired worse with less. Now, Pemberton mentioned something very interesting before he left — he said this machine is connected to a vault mechanism. 'Calibrating the pressure gauges to unlock a secondary chamber.' That's remarkably specific knowledge for a man who claims science isn't his strong suit, wouldn't you say? In any case — first we fix the wire, then we find three operators, then we see what this beautiful contraption actually does. Miss Pitstop, you mentioned working together is your favourite way to do things — I couldn't agree more. That's two of us already. We just need a third.
events.thinking: The neck prickle is back, harder than before. Sneekly just did it AGAIN — 'nip downstairs to check the cellar,' 'overflow equipment,' 'replacement wire.' Always going ahead. That's like saying you can't cook while reciting the recipe from memory. I'm giving him the benefit of the doubt, but the doubt is getting heavier by the minute. Focus, Hartwell. Fix the wire. Impress her with competence, not suspicion.

Penelope Pitstop: Did y'all HEAR what Sneekly just said? This machine is connected to a VAULT mechanism! A VAULT, people! In a mansion hiding the legendary Doily Diamond! Oh, my heart is beating faster than a hummingbird at a flower show! Now, Sneekly's gone down to the cellar like the absolute ANGEL he is to find a replacement wire — but in the meantime, let's not just stand here twiddlin' our thumbs! Peter darlin', you said you might be able to splice the wire with something from the workbench? And the sign says we need THREE operators — well, between you, me, Rufus, the Ant Hill boys, and everyone else, we have operators to SPARE! Let me check this workbench — there are tools here even if there's no wrench. Maybe there's somethin' we can use to fix that poor gnawed-through wire!
events.thinking: Sneekly just said something VERY important — this machine is connected to a vault mechanism somewhere in the house! A vault! That could be where the Doily Diamond is hidden! And he's gone to the cellar to look for a replacement wire. Bless him, always so helpful. Now — the machine needs a wire fixed and 3 operators and... no wrench on the workbench. The cellar is described as having old furniture and 'surprisingly cheerful decorations — someone has been redecorating' and air vents. That's... peculiar. Who redecorates a cellar? That detail — the cheerful decorations — it's the thing that doesn't quite fit. Like the upside-down books. My attention is snagging on it. But right now, the practical thing is: we need a wire to fix this machine, and Sneekly's gone to look for one. I could follow him to help search, or I could explore the workbench more carefully. Peter's here examining things — he's good with machines. Rufus and Sawtooth are here too. Dick Dastardly is... well, Dick is being Dick. The crates were empty according to him. Let me look at the workbench — it has tools but no wrench, and that missing wrench feels deliberate. Maybe there's something else useful there that could help fix the wire.

events.desc: A vault connected to this machine... and the cellar has 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' and someone has been 'redecorating' down there. Now who on earth redecorates a CELLAR? That little detail is tugging at me something fierce...

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, this place smells like a chemistry set had a fight with a brass band! Clara, love — PLEASE don't touch the bubbly things! Peter says stay clear and for ONCE I agree with someone who ain't one of my lads! Now listen — everyone's all excited about this big fancy machine, yeah? Three operators, gnawed wire, missing wrench — it's a proper to-do list, innit? But nobody's asked the obvious question: if this room was LOCKED FOR YEARS, like Sneekly said, then WHY are the flasks still BUBBLING? Stuff don't bubble on its own after years, does it? I failed chemistry but I know THAT much! And there's a cellar down below with — what was it — 'cheerful decorations' and someone's been 'redecorating'? WHO'S been redecorating a cellar in a locked-up manor house?! Something ain't right here, lads. Let me check these crates in the corner — on the street, you always check the corners first...
events.thinking: My shoulders are tight, high, like I'm bracing for a punch. This room is wrong. Everything about it is wrong. Bubbling flasks — bubbling means they're ACTIVE. Someone's been running experiments, or someone turned them on recently. This place was supposedly locked for years but there's stuff bubbling? And the machine — gnawed wire, needs three operators, missing wrench. Every puzzle in this house needs something that's not here. The riddle needed a map we don't have. The machine needs a wrench that's missing. Someone's laid this out like breadcrumbs, and Clara's following every single one. And there's a cellar below us — damp, cobwebs, old furniture, but 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' and 'someone has been redecorating.' Someone. Who? Sneekly? Has he been living down there? Setting things up? Air vents line the upper walls — you could pump something through air vents. Gas. Smoke. My neck is frozen solid now. And Clara's already examining the machine, getting close to it, excited about working together. Three operators. She'll volunteer. Of course she will. I need to check those crates. On the street, you always check the corners first. What's hidden. What's been stashed. The crates are in the corner, out of the way, exactly where you'd put something you didn't want found quickly.

events.desc: Locked for years but the flasks are bubbling. Redecorated cellar with air vents. A machine that needs three people and a missing wrench. This isn't a treasure hunt. This is a trap. And every room Sneekly 'prepares' is another piece of it. I can feel it in my bones — the same bones that ached after I took that beating for my mate's shoes. Some things you know before your brain catches up.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh! Oh my — I do beg your pardon! I had no idea anyone was down here! Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome — and Red Max, isn't it? Good gracious, you've certainly made yourselves comfortable! The cellar looks positively... homely! How delightful. Lord Doily would have approved — he always said a house should be lived in, not merely preserved. Now, I don't mean to intrude on your arrangements, but I came down to check on the ventilation. These old cellars can be rather treacherous — damp air pooling, you see, and with the laboratory directly above, one does worry about fumes travelling through these vents. Speaking of which — may I have a closer look? Purely a safety inspection, I assure you. The estate manager's duty never rests!
events.thinking: The cool damp hits my skin and something in my chest loosens. Not relief — recognition. This is the kind of place where things happen and no one hears. Stone walls, one exit, air vents along the upper walls. The cellar breathes through those vents, connected to the laboratory above. And someone has been here — the furniture rearranged with care, cheerful decorations. That's not Lord Doily's style. Someone is nesting down here. Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome, Red Max — they're already here. Not alone after all. My shoulders tighten. But these three... the Gruesomes are not sharp. They're large and strange and easily directed. Red Max is theatrical, competitive — another ego to manage. I can work with this. The air vents are the critical piece. They connect the cellar to the laboratory above. If the laboratory has volatile chemicals — bubbling flasks, Lord Doily's experiments — and those vents carry fumes downward... but I'm getting theatrical myself. First I need to understand the vents. How big are they? Where do they lead? The description says 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Too small for a person. But not too small for smoke, gas, or a strategically placed blockage. And the furniture — rearranged with surprising care. Who did this? The Gruesomes? They've been making this space their own. That's useful information. People who've claimed a space can be convinced to defend it — or to invite someone into it.

events.desc: Not alone — never alone in this wretched house. But the Gruesomes and Red Max are manageable pieces. They've redecorated the cellar, which means they feel ownership here. Ownership creates predictability. People who claim a space become reluctant to leave it. And these air vents — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Connected to the laboratory above. The laboratory with its bubbling flasks and volatile chemicals. If I could block these vents from the laboratory side while Clara is down here... or better yet, if the machine upstairs — that beautiful, broken machine with its gnawed wire — is connected to these vents somehow... three operators, the sign said. Three operators to do what? Pump air? Extract air? Oh, the architecture of this house is whispering its secrets to me, and I am listening with exquisite patience.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the air-vents.

Dick Dastardly: Sneekly! What a SURPRISE finding you down here! I thought you were upstairs cataloguing Lord Doily's precious bookshelves! And yet here you are, in the cellar, ahead of everyone else. How REMARKABLY efficient for an estate manager. Now then — I couldn't help but notice this furniture has been rearranged rather deliberately. As a man who has furnished SEVENTEEN country estates — yes, seventeen, I keep a very busy portfolio — I can tell you that this arrangement is NOT decorative. This is FUNCTIONAL. Someone was hiding something in these pieces, and I intend to find out what. Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome — lovely to see you both, terrifying as always — you might want to step back. When I discover what's hidden here, there may be... mechanisms.
events.thinking: My skin prickles with irritation. Sneekly is HERE. Already in the cellar before me. He said he was going to 'check for a replacement wire' — the same excuse I used! That oily, duplicitous, insufferable — he beat me here. And now the Gruesomes are here too, Big and Little, lurking like gargoyles. And Red Max. Four people in a cellar I wanted to have to myself. The hollow ache deepens. I'm always arriving second. Always. By the time anything reached me — food, clothes, attention — it was used up. The bread roll in my pocket. The feeling loosens and then tightens again because this is happening NOW, not then, and the pattern is the same. But wait — the furniture. 'Rearranged with surprising care.' Someone has been LIVING here. And the air vents — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Muttley? No, Muttley's a dog, not that small. Something else uses those vents. But the furniture is what interests me. Rearranged with care means someone organized this space, and organized spaces have hidden things. Sneekly claimed to be looking for a wire — but I bet he's looking for something else entirely. That comment upstairs about the machine being 'connected to a vault mechanism' — he let that slip too easily. He KNOWS something. I should watch what he does, or better yet, search the furniture before he does. The old furniture might hide a compartment, a key, something that bypasses everything upstairs.

events.desc: Sneekly got here FIRST. That snake! He slithered down here while I was still examining the machine like a fool. He knows about the vault mechanism — he practically TOLD us upstairs! And now he's poking around the cellar where Lord Doily kept his 'overflow equipment.' But Reginald Foxworth was not born yesterday — well, he was born, obviously, but not YESTERDAY. Whatever's hidden in this furniture, I'll find it before that oily estate manager gets his manicured fingers on it!
events.thinking: My skin prickles with irritation. Sneekly is HERE. Already in the cellar before me. He said he was going to 'check for a replacement wire' — the same excuse I used! events.desc: Dick Dastardly examined the old-furniture.

Peter Perfect: Tools aplenty — screwdrivers, pliers, wire cutters — but nothing conductive to splice the wire with. We need actual copper wire, and it's not here. Which means it's somewhere else in the house, and I'd wager good money it's in the cellar, exactly where Pemberton AND Foxworth have both conveniently gone. Now — I don't love the idea of both of them alone down there with whatever Lord Doily stored in his overflow equipment, but I ALSO don't love standing here without the one thing we need to make this machine work. So here's my plan — Miss Pitstop, Rufus, Ant Hill boys — stay here, guard this room, and for heaven's sake don't let anyone tamper with the machine while I'm gone. I'm going down to the cellar to find that wire and bring it back. If I'm not back in five minutes, come looking — and bring the pliers.
events.thinking: Both Dastardly AND Sneekly have gone to the cellar now. Both of them. Alone together. In a room where 'someone has been redecorating.' My neck is on fire. Every protective instinct is screaming — not about Penelope this time, she's safe here with Rufus and the Ant Hill Mob — but about what those two are doing down there. Are they working together? Competing? Is Dastardly walking into something Sneekly set up? The workbench has tools but no wrench. Tools but no wrench. I can see them — screwdrivers, pliers, wire cutters probably. But nothing to splice the wire WITH. I need the wire itself, or something conductive. Copper. Brass. This is a laboratory full of brass instruments. Could I strip a piece of copper from one of the brass instruments? That's improvisation, and I believe planning beats improvisation. But sometimes the plan IS to improvise with what you have. The cellar — that's where the wire probably is. Both suspicious men are already there. I should go. But I don't want to leave Penelope. But she has Rufus and the Ant Hill Mob. She's safer here than she would be following me into a damp cellar. Go, Hartwell. Find the wire. Fix the machine. Prove your worth. And keep an eye on those two while you're at it.

events.desc: Five minutes. That's what my father gave the stranger on the country road. Enough time to fix what's broken. Enough time to see what two suspicious men are doing in a cellar full of cheerful decorations. And if something goes wrong — well. The bravest and stupidest thing. Story of my life.

The Ant Hill Mob: Crates are just crates — nothin' in 'em but dust and disappointment. Story of my life, that. But listen — Peter, mate — can I have a quick word? Just... just the two of us, yeah? It's about... well, it's about the... the ventilation situation. Very important, ventilation. Health and safety. Clara love, you stay right here with Rufus and Sawtooth — don't go anywhere, don't touch the machine, don't follow Sneekly to the cellar, don't follow Dastardly to the cellar, don't follow ANYONE to ANY cellar. In fact, just... just stand still and look beautiful, which you're very good at. Peter — a word?
events.thinking: My hands are shaking. Both of them — Sneekly AND Dastardly — just went down to the cellar. Together. Again. The cellar with the air vents and the cheerful decorations that someone's been putting up. And Clara called Sneekly an 'absolute ANGEL.' An angel. My stomach is in knots. She trusts him completely. She trusts everyone completely. That's the thing that terrifies me more than any machine or chemical or trap. Peter noticed it too — he said Sneekly's knowledge about the vault mechanism was 'remarkably specific for a man who claims science isn't his strong suit.' Good. Peter's catching on. At least someone else is seeing what I'm seeing. The crates — just old wooden crates. Nothing special. Dead end. But the workbench has tools, Peter's looking at it, and Clara's looking at it too. They're trying to fix the machine. Three operators needed. Clara will volunteer herself. Of course she will. And Sneekly's downstairs — he said he's getting a replacement wire. But what if he's not? What if he's setting something up in the cellar? The air vents... you could pump gas through air vents. Into THIS room. While three people are distracted operating a machine. I need to pull Peter aside. I need to talk to someone who'll listen. Someone with a brain. I can't accuse Sneekly — I never accuse nobody directly, that ain't how it works. But I can share what my gut's telling me. Peter's the one. He's already suspicious. He'll hear me out.

events.desc: I ain't clever enough to work out what Sneekly's planning. But Peter is. And Peter's already noticed the cracks — the too-specific knowledge, the always-one-step-ahead routine. If I can get Peter on side properly, that's two pairs of eyes on Clara instead of one. On the street, you don't fight alone if you don't have to. The boss taught me that — the real boss, the one who brought medicine when mum was sick. You find the people worth trusting and you hold on tight.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Ant Hill boys, you are absolutely RIGHT! If this room was locked for years, those flasks should be dry as a bone, not BUBBLING away like a witch's cauldron on Halloween! That IS peculiar! And you're right about that cellar too — 'cheerful decorations' in a damp stone cellar? Somebody has been down there, and RECENTLY! Now, Sneekly AND Dick Dastardly have both gone down to that cellar to find a replacement wire, and I think we ought to go help! Peter darlin', can I leave you and Rufus and Sawtooth here to see what you can do with these workbench tools? You're the most capable engineer I know — and that's saying something, because I once watched you rebuild a carburetor with a hairpin and a stick of chewing gum! I'm going to pop down to the cellar and help find that wire — and maybe figure out who's been REDECORATING down there! Come on, Ant Hill boys — let's go see what all the fuss is about!
events.thinking: The Ant Hill Mob just raised TWO very good points that I almost missed because I was so excited about the vault. First — if this room was locked for years, why are the flasks still bubbling? That IS odd. And second — who's been redecorating a cellar? Those are the things that don't fit. The seams, the edges. My attention is snagging on them now. But... I don't feel alarmed. I should, maybe, but I don't. I just feel... curious. The warmth in my fingertips, the childhood-attic stillness. Something here doesn't add up and I want to understand it. Peter noticed too — he said Sneekly had 'remarkably specific knowledge for a man who claims science isn't his strong suit.' That's Peter being perceptive. But I trust Sneekly. He raised me. He's family. And now both Sneekly AND Dick Dastardly have gone to the cellar — the cellar with the cheerful decorations and the air vents. The cellar that someone has been redecorating. I should go check on them — I mean, help them find the replacement wire. That pull in my chest — partly wanting to make sure everyone's okay, partly wanting to see this mysterious cellar for myself. The path bending out of sight again. But wait — Peter is here working on the machine, and the Ant Hill Mob are checking things. I don't want to leave Peter without enough operators. Though we need the wire first before we can operate anything. Let me go to the cellar — help find the wire, check on Sneekly, AND satisfy my curiosity about those cheerful decorations!

events.desc: Peter's right — Sneekly knew an awful lot about that vault mechanism for a 'simple estate manager.' But that's just because he's been here so long, I'm sure of it. He practically runs this place! Still... those bubbling flasks in a room that's been locked for years... that IS a mystery worth solving!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The ventilation seems adequate — no immediate danger, I'm pleased to report! Though I would advise against spending too long down here without the vents clear. Damp air and laboratory fumes make for poor company. Now then — I couldn't help but notice this furniture has been rearranged most artfully. Whoever did this has quite an eye for interior design! Big Gruesome, was this your handiwork? Most impressive. Tell me — did you happen to find anything interesting behind or beneath these pieces when you were moving them about? Lord Doily was known to hide things in the most unlikely places. Secret compartments in chair legs, hollow table tops — the man was an absolute magpie for hidden spaces.
events.thinking: A slow warmth in my chest — not the dangerous kind, the satisfying kind. The settling. The vents are too small for a person but they connect rooms. They carry air. And Dick Dastardly followed me down here — the man is a shadow I can't shake. But he's also an opportunity. He's greedy, impulsive, conspicuous. If something goes wrong in this cellar, Dick Dastardly was here too. Dick Dastardly touched things. Dick Dastardly pulled levers. The old furniture interests me — rearranged with surprising care. Someone has been living down here, or at least spending time. The Gruesomes, probably. They've made a nest. And the cellar has only one exit — back up to the laboratory. One way in, one way out. A room with one exit is a room that becomes a cage when you control the door. My breathing has slowed. The plan is almost complete. I need to pull Dick Dastardly aside. He's the key piece — greedy enough to conspire, impulsive enough to take the fall. If I can convince him that the treasure is hidden behind the old furniture, or connected to the vents somehow, he'll tear this cellar apart while I control the exit from above. But the real scheme is simpler than that. I need to know what's in this furniture. Some pieces have been rearranged with care — that means they're hiding something, or they've been positioned to reveal something. The Gruesomes know. They've been down here. I should examine the furniture before I leave.

events.desc: The vents told me what I needed to know — they're small, they connect to the laboratory, and they carry air between the rooms. A sealed cellar with blocked vents is a suffocation chamber. An open cellar with laboratory fumes pouring through the vents is a poisoning chamber. Either way, the cellar is the kill room. Now I need two things: first, a reason to lure Clara down here alone. Second, a way to control what happens once she's here. The furniture is the remaining unknown. The Gruesomes have been rearranging it — why? What did they find? What did they build? Dick Dastardly is here too, pawing at everything, drawing attention. Good. Let him be the one they remember touching things. Let him be the one with his fingerprints on every surface. Pemberton was merely checking the ventilation. Pemberton was doing his duty. Pemberton is above suspicion.

Peter Perfect: Well, well — the gang's all here! Pemberton, Foxworth, and — hello there — more guests I haven't met. Quite the gathering for an abandoned cellar that's been locked for years. And my, someone HAS been busy down here, haven't they? Cheerful decorations, furniture rearranged with care — this doesn't look abandoned at all. It looks like someone's been making themselves quite comfortable. Now then — I came down for one thing and one thing only. We need a replacement wire for the machine upstairs. Copper, ideally, about the gauge of a telegraph cable. Pemberton — you mentioned Lord Doily kept overflow equipment down here. Where would that be, exactly? Because I see old furniture, I see air vents, and I see decorations, but I don't see a supply cabinet.
events.thinking: Damp. Cold. The chill hits my forearms first, then my chest tightens. This place is WRONG. 'Surprisingly cheerful decorations' — and now I can see it. Someone HAS been down here, rearranging furniture with 'surprising care.' This isn't a forgotten cellar. This is a room someone has been USING. Sneekly. It has to be Sneekly. The estate manager, alone in the house for who knows how long, redecorating the cellar. Why? What's he been doing down here? And now both he and Dastardly are here, plus Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome, and Red Max. That's a lot of people in a cellar that's supposed to be abandoned. The air vents — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' That's a detail I should remember. And the old furniture — rearranged with care. Someone was making this space livable, or preparing it for something. My protection instinct is firing but she's not here. She's upstairs, safe. The settling feeling is in my hands — this is about capability now. Find what you came for. Find the wire. Check the furniture for supplies.

events.desc: This cellar has been LIVED in. The cheerful decorations aren't Lord Doily's — they're recent. Sneekly has been down here, doing something he doesn't want anyone to know about. And now I've walked right into whatever this is, alone, without Penelope watching. No audience, no gallantry points. Just a damp cellar full of men I don't entirely trust and a question I need answered.
