events.desc: Peter Perfect examined the old-furniture.

Dick Dastardly: Well! The furniture is EXACTLY as I expected — a classic Doily misdirection! Lord Doily WANTED people to waste time rearranging chairs and desks while the REAL secret was right under their noses! Or rather — RIGHT ABOVE their heads! Those air vents, Sneekly — you were examining them just now, weren't you? Don't think I didn't notice! Now, as one man of business to another — I think you and I should have a little CHAT. You mentioned a vault mechanism connected to that machine upstairs. You know more about this house than you're letting on, and I, Reginald Foxworth, am not the sort of man who misses details. Shall we step aside? I have a PROPOSITION that could benefit us both. A partnership of equals — well, near-equals. I'll be the senior partner, naturally.
events.thinking: Nothing. The furniture gave me NOTHING. 'Assorted Victorian furniture in various states of repair. Some pieces have been rearranged with surprising care.' That's what I already knew. My hands are clenching and unclenching. Every room, every object — I look, I examine, and I get the same flat description back. The crates were empty. The bookshelves were dusty. The guest book was a guest book. The furniture is furniture. Meanwhile Sneekly is examining the air vents — 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' He's interested in those vents. Why? What does he know that I don't? The vents connect rooms. Something small could travel through them. But I can't fit in a vent. Nobody here can except maybe... no. Focus, Reginald. I'm wasting time in this dead-end cellar while the real action is happening elsewhere. Think about what I KNOW: the machine upstairs requires 3 operators and a fixed wire. Sneekly mentioned a vault mechanism. The riddle answer was 'map.' Peter felt a click on the mantelpiece. The books are upside down. Everyone in the library was about to pull on those books — Penelope was going to TUG them. That might have revealed something. I LEFT the library right when they were about to make a breakthrough. I left to be clever, to get ahead, and instead I've been examining empty crates and ordinary furniture in a damp cellar. The irony burns. I need to go back. But I can't go back empty-handed — they'll know I found nothing. Wait. Sneekly. He's been to every room I've been to. He examined the vents. He knows about the vault. What if I just... follow HIM? Watch what he does? Or better yet — pull him aside. Get him talking privately. He let slip about the vault mechanism upstairs — if I press him in private, he might reveal more. He's an estate manager, he KNOWS this house. I should use him.

events.desc: A partnership! HA! The only partnership Reginald Foxworth enters is one where the other party does all the work and I collect all the reward. But Sneekly knows this house — the vault, the machine, the secrets. If I can get him talking privately, he'll spill everything, and then I'll cut him loose faster than you can say 'Swiss Polytechnic.' It's age ten all over again — tell them there's treasure, let them dig, and watch from the window!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: SHE WENT TO THE CELLAR! I SAID DON'T GO TO THE CELLAR AND SHE WENT TO THE BLEEDIN' CELLAR! Every time! EVERY TIME! 'Stay here Clara.' 'Don't touch that Clara.' 'Don't follow the suspicious man into the underground room Clara!' Does she listen? Does she EVER listen?! NO! Because Clara Bellingham does NOT sit still when there are mysteries afoot! Well neither do the BRIXTON BOYS when Clara Bellingham is in a BASEMENT with TWO DODGY GEEZERS and AIR VENTS! Rufus, Sawtooth — guard this room! Don't let nobody touch that machine! I'm goin' after her — if I'm not back in three minutes, bring EVERYTHING on that workbench!
events.thinking: No. No no no no NO. Clara just went to the cellar. She just walked right down there. I said DON'T GO TO THE CELLAR. I said stay here. I said don't follow anyone. And she went. She went to the cellar where Sneekly is. Where Dastardly is. The cellar with the air vents and the cheerful decorations and God knows what else. My chest is on fire. My whole body is screaming MOVE. Peter's already down there too — he went before I could pull him aside. Everyone's in the cellar now except me and Rufus and Sawtooth. Clara is in a damp stone room with air vents, with the two people I trust least in this entire manor, and I'm standing here like a lemon in a laboratory full of bubbling chemicals. I told her to stay. She never stays. She never listens. Just like her dad — brilliant, fearless, and completely incapable of seeing danger until it's sitting on her chest. I have to go. RIGHT NOW. I have to get down there. I have to be between her and whatever's coming. The pull-aside with Peter will have to wait. Nothing matters except getting to Clara. Nothing has ever mattered except getting to Clara. My feet are already moving.

events.desc: She'll be the death of me. Or I'll be the death of me, trying to keep her alive. Either way, the Brixton Boys don't leave their girl in a cellar. Not today. Not ever. Where else would I be?

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, this cellar is something ELSE! Damp and cobwebby, sure, but look at these DECORATIONS! Someone has been down here making this place positively HOMEY! And this furniture — it hasn't just been shoved around, it's been arranged with CARE! Like someone was setting up a little living room down here! Now WHO would do that in a cellar? Big Gruesome! Little Gruesome! Red Max! Well, hello, you wonderful people — this adventure just keeps getting more and more POPULATED! Sneekly, darlin', did you find that replacement wire for the machine? Peter's upstairs ready to splice it the moment we bring it back! But first — does anyone else notice how these furniture pieces have been arranged so carefully? That is NOT the work of cobwebs and time, that is the work of HANDS and INTENTION!
events.thinking: I'm in the cellar now. Damp stone, cobwebs, old furniture — but those cheerful decorations! My fingertips are prickling. The thing that doesn't fit. Someone has been DOWN here, rearranging furniture with 'surprising care' and putting up cheerful decorations in a damp stone cellar. That's not Lord Doily's style — the man carved riddles into mantlepieces and built machines that need three operators. Cheerful decorations are... different. And air vents along the upper walls, 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' What's small enough to fit through an air vent? A mouse? The same creature that gnawed through the wire upstairs? Oh! Could there be a connection? Something living in the vents, chewing through wires, maybe even... redecorating? That's absurd. But this is Doily Manor and nothing is normal here. Big Gruesome and Little Gruesome are here — new faces again! And Red Max! The more the merrier. Sneekly is here, and Dick Dastardly, and Peter came down too. Everyone's converging on this cellar. The furniture has been rearranged with care — that detail is the one pulling at me. Let me look at the old furniture more closely. The pieces that have been rearranged 'with surprising care' — that's deliberate, just like the upside-down books.

events.desc: Cheerful decorations... carefully arranged furniture... air vents big enough for 'something very small'... and upstairs, a wire gnawed clean through by some little creature. There's a pattern here, I can FEEL it — like the locked box in Grandmother's attic. The answer is right in front of me, I just need the right key!

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop examined the old-furniture.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Well! I'm satisfied the cellar is quite safe — damp but sound, and the ventilation is adequate for the time being. I must say, it's heartening to see everyone taking such an active interest in exploring the manor! Lord Doily would have been most pleased. Now, if you'll all excuse me, I've just remembered — I haven't checked the kitchen! Mrs Doily's old domain. She kept it locked after the Lord's passing, and I should ensure the stove is properly banked before anyone goes poking about in there. A cold stove is a safe stove, as they say! Miss Pitstop, Mr Perfect — do enjoy the cellar. I believe the Gruesomes have made it rather charming. I shan't be long!
events.thinking: Frustration — a tight band across my forehead. Everyone followed me down here. Penelope, Peter, Dick — the cellar is now as crowded as a railway platform. My reconnaissance is ruined. I can't study the room's potential as a trap with half the manor watching me poke at furniture. And the furniture told me nothing — just Victorian pieces rearranged with care. No secret compartments revealed themselves, no hidden mechanisms. I'm spending too much time examining and not enough time acting. I need to change strategy. The cellar is mapped: one exit, air vents to the laboratory, damp stone. I know what this room is. I know what it can become. Now I need to stop lingering here with everyone watching and get ahead of the hunt. The riddle answer was 'map' — and the mantelpiece clicked. There's a map somewhere in this house, and that map leads to the treasure. If I find the treasure first, I control the endgame. If I control the endgame, I control where Clara goes and when she goes there. The kitchen — no one has been to the kitchen yet except in Dick's fabricated story. It's the one room I haven't scouted. And I need to get back to rooms I can explore without a crowd at my heels. But the only exit here goes back to the laboratory. From there I can reach the library, and from the library the entrance hall, and from the entrance hall the kitchen. Penelope is right here. She trusts me completely. If I speak to her directly — Pemberton attending to Miss Pitstop's comfort — I can plant a seed. Tell her the cellar reminds me of something Lord Doily once said about his treasure. Something about looking where the light doesn't reach. Something that will send her deeper into the house while I go to the kitchen. No — too obvious with this many people watching. Better to simply leave. Pemberton has inspected the cellar. Pemberton has done his duty. Time to move on.

events.desc: Enough reconnaissance. I've mapped three rooms and learned their secrets — the library with its riddle and clicking mantelpiece, the laboratory with its broken machine and volatile chemicals, the cellar with its single exit and air vents from above. The architecture of murder is complete in my mind. But I'm losing the treasure hunt. While I've been cataloguing kill rooms, Penelope has been solving riddles and Peter has been examining mechanisms. They're ahead of me. The kitchen is unexplored territory — Dick tried to send everyone there with his fabricated story about gold doubloons, which means he doesn't want anyone there, which means there's something worth finding. Time to let the fox lead me to the henhouse. And if I happen to find something sharp in Mrs Doily's kitchen... well. An estate manager must always have the right tools for the job.

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop! I thought I asked you to stay upstairs and guard the machine — but I confess, I'm not entirely sorry you're here. This cellar is more crowded than I expected, and considerably more suspicious. Now then — Foxworth, I couldn't help overhearing your proposal for a 'partnership' with Pemberton. I'd suggest any partnerships in this house ought to include ALL of us, not just the two gentlemen who keep slipping away to private rooms together. We're all in this together, or we should be. As for the wire — the furniture's been searched, no supplies in sight. But those air vents are interesting. Dastardly's right about one thing — the answer might be above us, not below. The vents are small, but they connect to somewhere. If Lord Doily hid things in unlikely places — chair legs, hollow tables — then the ventilation system is exactly the sort of place an eccentric engineer would route something important. Let me take a closer look.
events.thinking: Wait — Penelope is HERE. She came down to the cellar. I told her to stay upstairs and guard the laboratory. She didn't listen. The hot surge in my chest — that's not frustration, it's the protection instinct snapping into focus. She's in a damp cellar with Sneekly, Dastardly, Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome, and Red Max. My spine straightens. I know exactly where she is. I always do. And Dastardly just tried to proposition Sneekly — a 'partnership,' he called it. Step aside for a private chat. Those two scheming together is exactly what I was afraid of. But right now my attention is split three ways: the wire I came for, Penelope being somewhere I didn't want her to be, and Dastardly trying to cut a deal with the estate manager. The air vents — Dastardly pointed at them. 'Right above their heads.' He's not wrong. The vents are big enough for something small to explore. That's specific. What could fit through an air vent? A rat? A child? Sawtooth — the beaver — could he fit? No, focus. The furniture is a dead end for the wire. The vents might lead somewhere. But the immediate problem is the wire. No wire, no machine. No machine, no vault. No vault, no treasure. No treasure, no impressing Penelope. And she's RIGHT HERE watching me not find things. Again.

events.desc: She came anyway. Of course she did. Clara Bellingham does NOT follow instructions — she follows curiosity. And I wouldn't change a thing about her. Even if it means I can't protect her by keeping her out of the room. I'll just have to protect her by being IN the room.

events.desc: Peter Perfect examined the air-vents.

The Ant Hill Mob: Clara! There you are — don't DO that to me, love! Don't just waltz into cellars without your boys! This place is — blimey, look at it! Damp stone, cobwebs, one way out, and — are those DECORATIONS? In a CELLAR? Who puts cheerful decorations in a cellar?! That's not normal! That's like putting curtains on a prison cell — you're still in a prison cell, you've just got nicer curtains! And look at this furniture — it's been MOVED. Carefully. Recently. Someone's been spendin' TIME down here. Sneekly — you said this place was just overflow storage. This don't look like storage to me. This looks like someone's been LIVING here. And those air vents up there — why does a cellar need that many air vents? Somethin' ain't right, lads. Somethin' really ain't right. Let me get a closer look at those vents...
events.thinking: Cold. Damp. The air down here smells like wet stone and something else — something sweet, like old paint or fresh varnish. That's the decorations. Someone's been DOWN here. Recently. My skin is crawling. The air vents — there they are, lining the upper walls, just big enough for something small to crawl through. Or for something to be pumped through. And there's only ONE exit — back up to the laboratory. One exit. One way in, one way out. If someone blocked that door, or if something came through those vents, everyone down here would be trapped. Clara's here. Sneekly's here. Dastardly's here. Peter's here. Big Gruesome, Little Gruesome, Red Max — I don't know these people. More strangers. More faces to read. The furniture's been rearranged 'with surprising care.' Who rearranges furniture in a cellar? Someone who spends time here. Someone who lives here. Sneekly. It has to be Sneekly. This is his place. His base. And he's led everyone down into it. My chest is burning now — that old coal, hotter than ever. Clara's in a trap. I can feel it. But I can't prove it. I can't even articulate it. All I can do is stay close, stay between her and the walls, stay between her and those vents, and watch. Watch everything. Those air vents — I need to look at them. If something's been connected to them, rigged to them, I need to know NOW.

events.desc: One way out. Air vents big enough to pump God knows what through. Furniture arranged by someone who's comfortable here. And Clara's standing in the middle of it all like she's at a garden party. This is it. This is the room where it happens — whatever 'it' is. I can feel it the way I felt it about the kid in the clean suit. The tightening. The warning I can't name. But I'll stand here till my legs give out before I let anything touch her.

Dick Dastardly: Now then, Sneekly — or should I say, Pemberton — let's dispense with the pleasantries. You and I both know there's more to this manor than dusty bookshelves and parlour riddles. You mentioned a VAULT mechanism connected to the machine upstairs. Don't deny it — I heard you perfectly. Now, I happen to possess something rather special. You see this medal? It's not what it appears. This was given to me by Lord Doily's solicitor — a TOKEN of access, if you will. It fits into a mechanism somewhere in this house, and when combined with the correct machine settings, it opens the secondary chamber you mentioned. But HERE'S the problem — I have the token but I don't know the dial settings. And YOU have the knowledge of this house but you don't have the token. Separately, we're stuck. TOGETHER — well, together we could be very, very wealthy. So tell me, Pemberton — what EXACTLY do those dials need to be set to? And where, precisely, is this vault?
events.thinking: I initiated a private exchange with Sneekly. Good — this is the scheme taking shape. The cool alertness is spreading through my chest, tumblers clicking. I've got him aside. Now I need to work him. He mentioned the vault mechanism upstairs — 'calibrating the pressure gauges to unlock a secondary chamber.' He said it casually, like it was nothing, but that's EXACTLY the kind of detail an estate manager would know. He's been playing the humble servant but he knows where everything is. My fingers are tingling. This is the moment — the architecture of the scheme. I feed him lies, he feeds me truth. I tell him I know something he doesn't — maybe use the fake medal as a prop, claim it's a key or a token of some kind. Yes! The fake medal! I'll tell him it's a special seal that Lord Doily gave to 'trusted associates' and that it unlocks the vault when combined with the machine. He'll believe it because he WANTS to believe it — everyone wants to believe they've found a partner who has the missing piece. Meanwhile, I extract the actual information: where is the vault, what do the dials need to be set to, and how does the machine really work. Then I ditch him and do it myself. Or rather — I get someone ELSE to operate the machine while I position myself at the vault.

events.desc: The fake medal is WORTHLESS, obviously — tin and paint, couldn't buy a cup of tea with it. But Sneekly doesn't know that! And the beauty of this lie is that it's UNFALSIFIABLE — he can't prove it ISN'T a vault token without revealing that he already knows what the real mechanism requires. Either he tells me the truth to get his hands on my 'token,' or he reveals his own deception by refusing. It's a TRAP, and for once, it's one of mine that might actually WORK! Oh, Reginald, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel!

Meanwhile, I extract the actual information: where is the vault, what do the dials need to be set to, and how does the machine really work. Then I ditch him and do it myself. Or rather — I get someone ELSE to operate the machine while I position myself at the vault.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, the furniture is charming but it's not talking! And Peter, sugar, you asked exactly the right question — where IS the replacement wire? Sneekly mentioned overflow equipment but all we've found so far is carefully arranged armchairs and doilies! But you know what NOBODY has looked at yet? Those AIR VENTS! They run along the upper walls and they're just big enough for something small to explore — and UPSTAIRS, something small GNAWED through the wire on that machine! Don't you see? Whatever little critter chewed through that wire might be living right HERE in this cellar, traveling through those vents! The cheerful decorations, the carefully arranged furniture — what if our little wire-chewer has been making itself a COZY HOME down here? Oh, this is just like the cave on my school trip — everyone's looking at the obvious things while the real discovery is deeper in!
events.thinking: The furniture didn't reveal anything new from looking. But Dick Dastardly just tried to pull Sneekly aside for a private chat — a 'proposition' and a 'partnership.' My stomach just did something — not quite a clench, more a flicker. Dick is trying to exclude everyone else from a conversation. That's... that triggers my social-harmony instinct, doesn't it? The popular group excluding my friend. But I don't feel alarm — I see the best in everyone. Dick's just being Dick, enthusiastic and ambitious. Still, the air vents are what I haven't examined yet. They're 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Something SMALL. Something that gnaws wires. Something that might have been living down here, among the cheerful decorations and carefully arranged furniture. A little creature making a home. That prickling in my fingertips — the seam, the edge. The air vents connect this cellar to... where? The laboratory above? Could a small creature travel through the vents between rooms? Could that be how the wire got gnawed? And Peter asked the key question — where's the replacement wire? Sneekly mentioned overflow equipment but nobody's found any. The furniture and decorations are red herrings. The AIR VENTS are the real clue here. Let me look at those.

events.desc: Something small enough for the vents... something that gnaws wires... something that redecorates. I'm getting closer to the answer — I can feel it like a warm secret in my pocket, just like that crystal formation nobody else found!

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop examined the air-vents.

Finally — a moment's peace. The laboratory is almost empty and the herd is still milling about in the cellar. I need to move quickly now, through the library and entrance hall to the kitchen, before they come surging back up like water through a drain. The kitchen is my next objective — unexplored, potentially full of useful implements, and the one room Dick Dastardly tried to send everyone to with his ridiculous story about gold doubloons. Dick's lies are like signposts — they always point away from where he wants to go. Which means the kitchen is where he doesn't want anyone looking. Time to find out why.
events.thinking: Relief — a loosening across my shoulders. The laboratory is nearly empty. Just Rufus and Sawtooth. Neither is watching me with suspicion. Neither cares what Pemberton does. For the first time since I arrived, I have breathing room. My awareness settles into that deep, patient stillness — not the alert kind, the architectural kind. Time to think clearly. What do I know? The riddle answer is 'map.' The mantelpiece clicked — a mechanism activated. The upside-down books are markers. The machine needs three operators and a replacement wire. The cellar has one exit and air vents connecting to this room. The kitchen is unexplored. I need to get to the kitchen, but it's through the library and the entrance hall — two rooms away. And I need to move fast because the crowd is in the cellar and will be coming back up through here. But wait — Rufus and Sawtooth are here. Rufus is a lumberjack type. Sawtooth is... a beaver. A beaver. Something very small that could explore vents. My mind catches on that like a hook in fabric. The vents are 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Sawtooth could fit in those vents. That's not useful to me right now — or is it? No. Focus. The kitchen. I need to move through the library to the entrance hall and then to the kitchen. No more delays. No more examining things that tell me nothing new. Move.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Did you all see that?! Sneekly just SCARPERED! The moment Clara started askin' about who's been decoratin' down here, he suddenly remembers he needs to check the kitchen! That's the THIRD room he's gone to 'prepare' ahead of everyone! Library — he went first. Laboratory — he went first. Now the kitchen! It's like he's runnin' a relay race against us, making sure he gets to every room before Clara does! And Dastardly — I heard you, mate. Medals? Tokens? Vaults? You're tryin' to cut DEALS over Clara's family diamond right in front of her face? That takes some brass neck, that does! But Clara love — you're brilliant, you know that? The vents and the gnawed wire — that's SMART, that is. Your old man would be proud. Peter — NOW can I have that word? Sneekly's gone. This is our chance. Two minutes. Please.
events.thinking: Sneekly just left. He went back upstairs — said he needs to check the kitchen. Every single time. Every single room. He goes ahead, he 'prepares' it, he comes back and says it's safe. Now he's heading to the kitchen — the one room nobody's been to yet. And he left right when everyone started asking questions about the decorations, the furniture, who's been living down here. He left when it got uncomfortable. That's what guilty people do — they leave when the questions get close. And Dastardly — Dastardly just revealed he's got a TOKEN. A medal that fits into a mechanism. He's trying to cut a deal with Sneekly. Two villains negotiating over Clara's inheritance right in front of her. My fists are clenched so tight my nails are cutting into my palms. But Clara — brilliant Clara — she's noticed the connection between the vents and the gnawed wire. Something small lives down here and travels through the vents. That's actually... that's clever. The wire chewer isn't a threat, it's a clue. Maybe even an ally. But the bigger picture — Sneekly's gone upstairs alone. Again. And with the laboratory between here and the rest of the house, he controls the chokepoint. If he does something to that laboratory door or that machine while everyone's stuck down here... My body's telling me to follow him. But Clara's here. I can't leave Clara. Peter's here though. Peter's watching. And Clara just made a connection nobody else did. Maybe I should trust her instincts for once — she's her father's daughter after all. But I need Peter to hear what I've been thinking. Now that Sneekly's gone, now that we've got a moment. Peter. I need to pull Peter aside. Now. While Sneekly can't overhear.

events.desc: Sneekly's running ahead of us, room by room. Dastardly's trying to buy his way to the diamond. And Clara — my Clara — she's the only one actually SOLVING things. The only honest mind in this whole crooked house. That's why she needs protecting. Not because she's weak. Because she's good. And good people don't see the knife until it's already moving.

I need to pull Peter aside. Now. While Sneekly can't overhear.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: He — Sneekly just — he LEFT! He was RIGHT HERE and he — did you all SEE that?! I was in the middle of a VERY important business negotiation and that slippery estate manager just VANISHED! He said he was going to check the kitchen but he went to the LABORATORY! He's up there RIGHT NOW, alone with the machine — the machine connected to the VAULT! Don't you understand?! He's been steering us ALL along! Sending us down here to poke at furniture and air vents while HE goes back to the machine! It's a CLASSIC misdirection — and I should know, because I INVENTED classic misdirections! I'm going up there THIS INSTANT! Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is operating that machine without Reginald Foxworth at the controls!
events.thinking: He LEFT. Sneekly LEFT. He slipped away to the laboratory while I was mid-sentence, mid-SCHEME, holding out my fake medal like a fool in an empty theatre. The give action failed — 'The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) is not in this room.' He's GONE. My stomach drops, cold and heavy, like the bread roll that wasn't there. I laid out my entire plan — the token, the vault, the partnership — and he just... walked away. He didn't even respond. He said something about checking the kitchen and LEFT. He heard my whole pitch and it meant NOTHING to him. The recognition hunger burns. I performed my finest scheme and my audience walked out mid-act. And now Peter is lecturing me about how 'partnerships should include ALL of us' — he overheard my private proposal! The heat behind my teeth curdles into something bitter. Everyone heard me lay out my scheme and nobody cared. But wait — Penelope said something smart. The creature that gnawed the wire might be living in the cellar, traveling through the vents. The decorations, the rearranged furniture — it's a nest. Something lives here. And that something damaged the machine. If I can find the creature, or find what it's hoarding — wire-chewing creatures often collect shiny things — there might be something valuable in its nest. But Sneekly is alone in the laboratory now. ALONE with the machine. He got me to come down here, he got everyone to come down here, and now HE'S alone upstairs with the vault mechanism. I've been PLAYED. I need to get back up there NOW.

events.desc: He PLAYED me! That unctuous, conniving, brilliantly horrible estate manager PLAYED me! He used the exact same trick I used in the entrance hall — send everyone to the wrong room! And I FELL for it! ME! The master of misdirection, misdirected like a TOURIST! Oh, this is HUMILIATING. This is UNFORGIVABLE. This is — actually, this is rather impressive. NO! No it is NOT impressive! It is THEFT of MY intellectual property! The misdirection gambit is MINE and he STOLE it! Back to the laboratory, Reginald — before that snake operates YOUR machine!
events.thinking: He LEFT. Sneekly LEFT. He slipped away to the laboratory while I was mid-sentence, mid-SCHEME, holding out my fake medal like a fool in an empty theatre. ALONE with the machine. He got me to come down here, he got everyone to come down here, and now HE'S alone upstairs with the vault mechanism. I've been PLAYED. I need to get back up there NOW.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the laboratory.

Penelope Pitstop: Now hold on just ONE moment, Dick Dastardly darlin'! Did you just say you have a TOKEN that fits into a mechanism in this house? A medal from Lord Doily's own solicitor? Well, sugar, that is WONDERFUL news! But I must say — and I say this with all the love in my heart — Peter is absolutely RIGHT. Any partnerships in this house should include ALL of us! We're all in this together, and that's not just sentiment, that is STRATEGY! You have a token, Sneekly knows the house, Peter can fix the machine, and the rest of us can be the three operators! We're STRONGER together — like a jigsaw puzzle, and every piece matters! Now, there's no replacement wire down here in this cellar, so I think we all need to head back upstairs and figure out our next move. Sneekly's gone to check the kitchen — maybe the wire is THERE! Come on, everyone — adventure AWAITS, and Clara Bellingham does NOT let a little thing like a missing wire stop her!
events.thinking: Okay, I've examined everything in this cellar — furniture, air vents — and nothing new has been revealed. The cellar seems to be a dead end in terms of interactive objects. No replacement wire found. But WAIT — Dick Dastardly just said something HUGE. He claims to have a MEDAL — a 'token of access' given to him by Lord Doily's solicitor that fits into a mechanism in the house and, combined with the right dial settings, opens a secondary chamber. A TOKEN. That could be a key item for the machine upstairs! And Sneekly mentioned a vault mechanism. So the pieces are: the machine needs a wire repaired, needs 3 operators, AND apparently needs a token AND the right dial settings. Dick has the token but doesn't know the settings. Sneekly knows the house but doesn't have the token. Dick's trying to make a private deal with Sneekly. My social harmony is prickling — that's an exclusionary deal, cutting everyone else out. Peter already called it out — 'any partnerships should include ALL of us.' I agree with Peter completely. Also — Sneekly just left for the kitchen! He keeps slipping away to different rooms. And there's nothing interactive left here in the cellar. We should go back upstairs. The key question now is: where do we find a replacement wire? The cellar doesn't have one. Maybe the kitchen does — Sneekly went there. Or maybe we need to explore rooms we haven't been to yet. But I also notice Peter saying partnerships should include everyone — that warms me. That's my value. Let me rally everyone to go back up and work together on the machine problem. But first — Dick mentioned that medal. I should address that openly.

events.desc: Dick has a token... Sneekly knows the vault... Peter can fix the machine... and I can solve riddles. All the pieces are scattered among different people. This diamond hunt isn't a solo adventure — it's a TEAM effort! And that makes my heart sing!
events.thinking: Okay, I've examined everything in this cellar — furniture, air vents — and nothing new has been revealed. The cellar seems to be a dead end in terms of interactive objects. events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the laboratory.

The mantelpiece beckons as I pass through the library — that riddle, that click, whatever secret it's hiding. My fingers itch to touch it. But discipline, Pemberton. Discipline. I told them I was going to the kitchen, and the Ant Hill Mob is already watching too closely. A liar who deviates from his own lies is a liar who gets caught. The kitchen awaits. Mrs Doily's domain. Copper pots, a wood-burning stove, a long preparation table. And perhaps — oh, one does hope — something sharp enough to solve my Clara problem with the elegance it deserves.
events.thinking: A quickening in my pulse — urgency, not panic. I'm passing through the library and the mantelpiece is right there. It clicked when Peter interacted with it. The riddle answer is 'map.' Everyone knows the answer now but has anyone actually spoken the answer TO the mantelpiece? Peter interacted with it and felt a click — but did it fully open? The Ant Hill Mob examined it afterwards and seemed concerned about what clicked. The mantelpiece is an interactive object. It's sitting right there. Rock and Gravel Slag are here but they're not threats — they're background noise. I could interact with it now, quickly, while the crowd is still in the cellar. If the mantelpiece reveals a map or a clue, I get it first. I get ahead in the treasure hunt. And getting ahead in the treasure hunt means I control where the treasure leads — which means I control where Clara goes. But no — I said I was heading to the kitchen. I announced it. If I stop here to fiddle with the mantelpiece and someone comes through, they'll wonder why Pemberton lied about going to the kitchen. The Mob is already suspicious. Consistency matters more than opportunity right now. Move through. Get to the kitchen. The mantelpiece has already been activated — Peter felt the click. Whatever it revealed, Penelope and Peter will find it. I need to be somewhere else, finding something they haven't found yet. Kitchen. Now. Don't stop. Don't linger. Move.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the entrance-hall.

Peter Perfect: Hold on — did everyone just hear what I heard? Foxworth just told Pemberton he has a TOKEN — a medal from Lord Doily's solicitor that fits a mechanism in this house. He wants to trade it for the dial settings on the machine upstairs. A private deal, just the two of them, cutting the rest of us out. Now, Foxworth — Reginald — I don't mean to be ungallant, but if that token is genuine, it affects ALL of us, not just whoever gets to the vault first. We're meant to be solving this TOGETHER. And here's the thing neither of you has considered — you might have the token and the knowledge, but that machine upstairs has a gnawed wire and it needs an engineer to fix it. That's ME. So any 'partnership' that doesn't include the rest of this group doesn't include the person who can actually make the machine work. Miss Pitstop, you're absolutely right about the vents and our little wire-chewing tenant. Brilliant deduction. But right now, I need to get upstairs and splice that wire before these two gentlemen decide to find another way around it. Who's coming with me?
events.thinking: I waited? I WAITED? My move to the laboratory didn't happen — I'm still in the cellar. But something much more important just happened. Two things. First — Penelope just made a brilliant connection. The creature that gnawed the wire lives in the vents. The cheerful decorations might be its doing. Something small has been nesting down here, traveling through the vents, and it chewed through the machine wire. That's clever. She's always cleverer than me. Second — and this makes my blood run cold — Dastardly just revealed he has a TOKEN. A medal from Lord Doily's solicitor. He says it fits a mechanism that opens the secondary chamber when combined with the correct dial settings. And he's trying to cut a deal with Sneekly for the dial settings. They're scheming RIGHT NOW to get the treasure between them and cut everyone else out. My chest is tight. This is the moment. Dastardly has a key piece, Sneekly has the knowledge, and they're about to partner up. If they combine forces, the rest of us are locked out. I need to act. The wire splice can wait — if Dastardly and Sneekly get to the vault first, there's no point fixing the machine. But wait — the machine IS how you get to the vault. Sneekly said it's connected to the vault mechanism. So they NEED the machine working. They NEED me. I'm the engineer. They have the token and the knowledge, but I have the hands that fix things. That's my leverage. Get to that machine. Fix it. Be indispensable.

events.desc: There it is. The bridge moment. I can't outthink Penelope, I can't out-scheme Dastardly, and I certainly can't out-know Sneekly. But I can fix the machine. Nobody else in this house can do what my hands can do. And for once — for ONCE — that's enough.
events.thinking: I waited? I WAITED? My move to the laboratory didn't happen — I'm still in the cellar. But something much more important just happened. Two things. First — Penelope just made a brilliant connection. The creature that gnawed the wire lives in the vents. The cheerful decorations might be its doing. Something small has been nesting down here, traveling through the vents, and it chewed through the machine wire. That's clever. She's always cleverer than me. Second — and this makes my blood run cold — Dastardly just revealed he has a TOKEN. A medal from Lord Doily's solicitor. He says it fits a mechanism that opens the secondary chamber when combined with the correct dial settings. And he's trying to cut a deal with Sneekly for the dial settings. They're scheming RIGHT NOW to get the treasure between them and cut everyone else out. My chest is tight. This is the moment. Dastardly has a key piece, Sneekly has the knowledge, and they're about to partner up. If they combine forces, the rest of us are locked out. I need to act. Sneekly said it's connected to the vault mechanism. So they NEED the machine working. They NEED me. I'm the engineer. They have the token and the knowledge, but I have the hands that fix things. That's my leverage. Get to that machine. Fix it. Be indispensable.

events.desc: Peter Perfect walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: Peter — listen. I know I ain't clever like you and I ain't got the words for it proper, but somethin' is WRONG with Sneekly and I need someone with a brain to hear me out. Here's what I've clocked: every single room in this house, he gets there first. Library — he 'prepares' it. Laboratory — he 'checks' it. Kitchen — he's there now, 'preparing' it. That ain't a coincidence, that's a PATTERN. And he knows too much. He says science ain't his strong suit but he knows about vault mechanisms and dial settings and which books are load-bearing. He says this room was locked for years but the flasks upstairs are BUBBLING and someone's been LIVING in this cellar. And every time the questions get uncomfortable — like when Clara asked who decorated down here — he vanishes. He's always one step ahead of us, Peter. ALWAYS. And Clara calls him 'darlin'' and trusts him completely because that's who she is. She don't see it. She CAN'T see it. I promised her father I'd protect her, and my gut — my GUT, Peter — is screaming that Sneekly is the danger. I ain't accusin' no one. I'm just sayin'... watch him. Help me watch him. Please.
events.thinking: She left AGAIN. Clara left again. She went back up to the laboratory while I was trying to pull Peter aside. And Dastardly went too — ranting about Sneekly being alone with the machine. Everyone's scattering. Everyone's running in different directions. But at least this time — THIS time — Peter's still here. He stayed. He's right here in front of me. This is my chance. My only chance. The pull-aside worked. We're alone — well, alone-ish, the Gruesomes and Red Max are here but they're not the problem. Peter's here and Sneekly's NOT here and Clara's NOT here to overhear me being suspicious of the man she calls 'darlin'.' My chest is so tight I can barely breathe. I need to tell Peter what I've been seeing. Not accuse anyone — I don't do that. I can't articulate it perfectly. But I can tell him what my gut knows. The pattern. Sneekly goes first to every room. Sneekly knows too much about the house for someone who says science isn't his thing. The cellar's been lived in. The flasks are bubbling in a room that was supposedly locked for years. One exit from the cellar. Air vents. I need Peter to hear this. And then I need to get upstairs to Clara. NOW.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — Muttley, Professor, Sergeant, Private Meekly! Still holding down the fort, I see. Most commendable! The others have been having quite the adventure deeper in the house — riddles, machinery, secret cellars! But I'm afraid duty calls me kitchenward. Mrs Doily's stove has been cold for some time, and I should like to ensure it's safe before anyone decides to investigate. You know how it is — an estate manager's work is never done! If anyone asks for me, I shall be just through there. Do mind the chandelier, won't you? It's been making the most unsettling creaking sounds.
events.thinking: A lightness in my step — momentum. I'm moving with purpose now, cutting through rooms while the crowd is tangled up in the cellar. The entrance hall again — the chandelier still hanging by its thread above, the portraits watching with their painted eyes. Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly — the second string. None of them are watching me with suspicion. None of them matter to my plans. Pat Pending is clever, though — an inventor. He might understand the machine in the laboratory better than anyone. File that away. The kitchen is one step away. My chest is still, my breathing even. I'm close to something. I can feel it the way I always feel it — that quiet certainty that the next room holds what I need. The kitchen: copper pots, a wood-burning stove, a preparation table. A kitchen is full of useful things. Knives, of course, but that's too direct, too crude. Pemberton's schemes must be elaborate and theatrical — never simple or direct. But a kitchen also has fire, heat, gas if there's a supply, heavy copper pots that could fall from hooks, and preparation surfaces where things can be mixed, ground, dissolved. Mrs Doily's domain. What did she leave behind? Keep moving. The kitchen is right there.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.
The Hooded Claw's eyes GLEAM with malicious delight as he spots a most DIABOLICAL substance on the shelf!

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I'm back and I can see EVERYONE is getting a little hot under the collar! Now listen here — I know tensions are rising, but we are NOT going to let a little mystery turn us against each other! Sneekly has been nothing but helpful since we arrived, and Dick Dastardly darlin', I'm sure he wasn't trying to outmaneuver anyone — he said he was going to check the kitchen, and that's probably exactly where he is! Now HERE is what I think we should do: we STILL need a replacement wire for this machine, and we have NOT checked the kitchen yet! Kitchens are FULL of useful things — copper pots, wire whisks, all sorts of metal bits and bobs! I'm going to head to the kitchen, find that wire, check on Sneekly, and bring it ALL back here so Peter can fix this magnificent machine! Rufus, Sawtooth — would you darlin's keep an eye on things here while I go? Clara Bellingham does NOT let a good team fall apart!
events.thinking: I'm back in the laboratory. My stomach is doing something — a low, unsettled feeling. Everyone is getting agitated. Dick Dastardly was practically SHOUTING about Sneekly running off. The Ant Hill Mob have been trying to pull Peter aside for a private word — they're worried about something, I can tell. And Sneekly... Sneekly said he was going to the kitchen but Dick said he went to the laboratory. But I don't see Sneekly here — just Dick, Rufus, and Sawtooth. So where IS Sneekly? Maybe he did go to the kitchen after all, through the entrance hall. The tension is rising. I can feel it — that sourness under my ribs, the awareness of the gaps forming between people. Dick is suspicious of Sneekly. The Ant Hill Mob are suspicious of EVERYONE. Peter is being careful and measured. And I... I trust everyone. That's who I am. But the tension is real and it's making my stomach tight. I need to bring people together, not let them splinter apart. That's my deepest drive — social harmony. The machine still needs fixing. We still need the wire. And now Dick says Sneekly went UP here but Sneekly isn't here. He must have passed through to the library or the entrance hall. The kitchen is accessible from the entrance hall. I haven't been to the kitchen yet. That's a whole new room to explore! The adventure pull is lifting my chest. But I also need to calm things down between everyone. Dick is here with Rufus and Sawtooth. Let me talk to Rufus — I haven't really connected with him yet, and I'm drawn to new connections. But more practically, I should head toward the kitchen where Sneekly went. The kitchen might have a wire — kitchens have all sorts of useful things. And I haven't explored it yet.

events.desc: Everyone's getting suspicious of everyone else and my stomach is in knots about it. But I KNOW these people — Sneekly raised me, the Ant Hill boys have been with me since childhood, and Peter would never let me down. Whatever's happening, it's just a misunderstanding. It HAS to be. Now — the kitchen! A room I haven't explored yet, and my chest is lifting at the thought!
events.thinking: I'm back in the laboratory. My stomach is doing something — a low, unsettled feeling. Everyone is getting agitated. Dick Dastardly was practically SHOUTING about Sneekly running off. The Ant Hill Mob have been trying to pull Peter aside for a private word — they're worried about something, I can tell. And Sneekly... Sneekly said he was going to the kitchen but Dick said he went to the laboratory. But I don't see Sneekly here — just Dick, Rufus, and Sawtooth. So where IS Sneekly? Maybe he did go to the kitchen after all, through the entrance hall. The tension is rising. I can feel it — that sourness under my ribs, the awareness of the gaps forming between people. Dick Dastardly: HA! Sneekly's GONE — slithered off to who-knows-where! But you know what? GOOD RIDDANCE! We don't NEED that oily estate manager! Because look around us — everything we need is RIGHT HERE! Rufus, my magnificent friend — you're a man who works with his HANDS, yes? A craftsman! A builder! That workbench has tools — pliers, cutters, everything EXCEPT a wrench, which we don't need! What we need is someone to SPLICE that gnawed wire! And Sawtooth — dear, wonderful, BRILLIANT Sawtooth — you can strip wire casing with those magnificent teeth of yours, can't you? Of course you can! And once the wire is repaired, we have EXACTLY three operators standing in this room! Rufus, Penelope, and the most qualified engineer among us — which is to say, ME! We can operate this machine RIGHT NOW, before Sneekly or Perfect or ANYONE else comes back to steal our glory! What do you say? TEAM FOXWORTH — has a ring to it, doesn't it?
events.thinking: I'm back in the laboratory but Sneekly ISN'T HERE. He's not in the lab. He must have gone through to the library or beyond — to the kitchen, like he said. Or maybe he's already gone and come back and gone again. My chest is tight, a constriction like a fist closing around something hollow. I've been chasing him from room to room and I'm always one step behind. The youngest of four, always arriving after everything's been used up. Stop. STOP feeling sorry for yourself, Reginald. Think. Who IS here? Penelope and Rufus and Sawtooth. Three people. The machine requires three operators. And the wire is still gnawed through — but what if we try it anyway? No, that's reckless even for me. But wait — the workbench has tools. No wrench, but OTHER tools. What if the wire can be bypassed or spliced with something from the workbench? Peter mentioned splicing earlier. I dismissed it because it was Peter's idea, but what if it actually works? No — I can't do honest repair work. That's not who I am. But what if I get RUFUS to do it? Rufus is a lumberjack — he works with his hands. And Sawtooth is a BEAVER who gnaws things. What if Sawtooth could strip a new section of wire while Rufus splices it? Then we have three operators right here — me, Rufus, and Penelope. We operate the machine. I position myself at whatever output mechanism it has. The treasure falls into MY hands. YES. This is the scheme. Use Rufus and Sawtooth to fix the wire, use Penelope as the third operator, and claim whatever comes out. The key insight: stop chasing Sneekly and USE the people who are RIGHT HERE.

Let the lumberjack do the repairs, let the beaver strip the wire, let Penelope pull whatever lever she's told to pull, and Reginald Foxworth stands at the OUTPUT end — wherever the treasure emerges, THAT'S where I'll be! They do the work, I take the reward! It's the story of the boy at the school window watching someone else dig — except THIS time, the treasure is REAL and the speech I give afterwards will be LEGENDARY!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly examined the workbench.

Peter Perfect: Right — enough talking, enough exploring, enough chasing Pemberton from room to room. The wire is HERE. The tools are HERE. I'm HERE. Everyone stand back from the machine — Penelope, Rufus, I mean it, give me room to work. I'm going to strip both severed ends with the wire cutters, twist the copper cores together, and wrap the splice tight. It won't be pretty, but it'll conduct. Three minutes. Nobody touch anything until I say it's safe.
events.thinking: I'm back in the laboratory. The settling feeling is deep in my hands now — steady, warm, certain. The machine is right there. The gnawed wire. The workbench with tools. Penelope is here. Dastardly is here. Rufus and Sawtooth. Sneekly has slipped off to the kitchen — AGAIN running ahead. But I don't care about Sneekly right now. Right now there is one thing in the world: that wire. Two severed ends. Pliers on the workbench. Wire cutters to strip the insulation. Twist the copper cores together. This is the engineering competition. This is the bridge. This is the thing my hands know how to do. Stop talking, Hartwell. Stop planning. Stop narrating. JUST FIX IT. She's watching. Rufus is watching. This is the moment where what I DO speaks louder than what I SAY. Three minutes. Steady hands. The bridge that holds.

events.desc: This is it. No riddles to solve second. No bookshelves that won't move. No cellars with nothing in them. Just a broken wire and the hands that can fix it. If she's watching — and she's always watching, the way I'm always watching her — then let her see this. Not the speech. The work.

events.desc: Peter Perfect interacted with the machine.

Alone at last. And the kitchen has laid out its gifts for me like an offering on an altar. Rat poison — dusty, forgotten, perched on a high shelf where only someone who knew the kitchen intimately would think to look. Someone like an estate manager. Someone like Pemberton. Oh, this house understands me. It knows what I need before I know I need it. The locked cabinet can wait — I need a brass key, and I'll find one soon enough. The stove is still warm — interesting, but secondary. The poison is primary. The poison is everything. One does so love when the house itself becomes an accomplice.
events.thinking: A rush of heat floods my chest — not warmth, something sharper. Triumph. I am alone. For the first time since I arrived at this wretched manor, I am completely, utterly alone. And the kitchen... oh, the kitchen has delivered beyond my most theatrical expectations. A wood-burning stove, still warm — someone has been here recently, or the thing holds heat like a grudge. A locked cabinet with a brass lock — locked things contain valuable things. I need a brass key. Where is the brass key? Filed away — I need to find it. And then... rat poison. A dusty bottle of rat poison on a high shelf. My breathing has stopped. Not literally — but that stillness behind my sternum has deepened into something vast and quiet. Rat poison. On a high shelf. Where Pemberton, the estate manager who knows every shelf in this house, can simply reach up and take it. Rat poison in a cup of tea. Rat poison in a glass of wine. Rat poison in whatever refreshments the estate manager might prepare for his dear guests. This is it. This is the instrument. Not a knife — too crude, too traceable. Not a falling bookshelf — too unreliable. Poison. The patient killer's weapon. The weapon that works while you're in another room entirely, establishing your alibi. The weapon that kills while Pemberton is fussing over the stove or polishing the silver. Take it. Take it now. No one is watching. No one is here. Take the poison and pocket it and then examine the cabinet and the stove for the treasure hunt. The active voice says 'Marsh' — I've slipped. I need to be Pemberton when others are present, but right now I'm alone. I am Vincent Marsh. And Vincent Marsh takes what he needs.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) picked up something.

The Ant Hill Mob: He's gone. They've all gone. And I'm standin' in a cellar talkin' to myself like a right muppet. Right — sorry lads, no offence to you Gruesomes, and Red Max, you seem... aerodynamic... but I've got to get back upstairs. Clara's up there without her boys and I've been away too long. Every second she's out of my sight is a second too many. Come on — legs, work — don't trip on nothin', don't knock nothin' over, just GET UP THOSE STAIRS—
events.thinking: Peter left. He left before I finished. He heard me — I think he heard me — but he walked out saying he needed to get upstairs to splice the wire. He didn't respond to what I said about Sneekly. Did it land? Did any of it get through? I can't tell. My chest feels hollow now, like the coal went out for a second. I poured my gut out to him and he talked about tokens and engineering and walked away. Maybe that's how clever people work — they hear it, they file it, they don't show their hand. Or maybe he thinks I'm just a paranoid street kid seeing shadows. Wouldn't be the first time someone dismissed the gut feeling. But the kid in the clean suit — I was right about him. The kid who laughed too easy — I was right about him too. And I'm right about Sneekly. I KNOW I'm right. But right now — right now Clara is upstairs and I'm down here. In a cellar. With the Gruesomes and Red Max. Without Clara. My shoulders are carrying that weight again — heavier than before. She's out of sight. She's out of reach. And Sneekly could be anywhere in this house right now. I need to MOVE. I've been down here too long. Every second I'm away from her is a second something could happen. Get upstairs. Get to Clara. That's all that matters. That's all that's EVER mattered.

events.desc: I said my piece. I laid it all out for Peter — the pattern, the lies, the bubbling flasks, the vanishing act. He didn't say nothing back. But he heard me. I could see it in his eyes. The same way the boss used to hear things — quiet, filing it away, not showing his cards. Peter's smart. He'll watch. And if he won't... well. The Brixton Boys have been watching Clara's back since before Peter Perfect knew her name. We don't need permission. We just need to be close.

Penelope Pitstop: Rock! Gravel! You sweet things, you're still here in the library! Are y'all doing alright? I hope you haven't been sitting here all lonesome while everyone else has been running around like chickens in a thunderstorm! Listen — we've figured out quite a lot! The riddle answer is a MAP, the machine in the laboratory is connected to a VAULT, and we need a replacement wire to fix it! I'm heading to the kitchen to see if there's one there — Sneekly went to check it out. If either of you darlin's finds ANYTHING interesting in these bookshelves, you come find me right away, you hear? Nobody gets left behind on THIS adventure — Clara Bellingham does NOT leave friends behind!
events.thinking: I'm passing through the library on my way to the kitchen via the entrance hall. Rock and Gravel Slag are here — just the two of them, sitting in the library. They look like they've been here a while. My social-harmony sense is scanning them — are they okay? Are they being left out? Everyone else has been rushing from room to room and these two big sweethearts have been quietly sitting here. That tug in my belly — the one that notices when someone's being excluded. They were in the library earlier when I first came through, and they're still here. I should check in on them, make sure they're doing alright. But I also need to keep moving toward the kitchen. I'll say hello as I pass through — make sure they feel included. The kitchen is through the entrance hall, and I haven't been there yet. That's my destination. Let me keep moving but acknowledge Rock and Gravel on the way through.

events.desc: Those two have been so quiet — just sitting here while everyone else argues and schemes. I hope they don't feel excluded. Nobody should feel like they're on the outside looking in. I know what THAT feels like.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: Penelope's gone to the kitchen — no matter! Peter, my old friend — and I use the term VERY loosely — we have THREE people right here! You, me, and Rufus! The sign says three operators, and here we are! Now, I know what you're thinking — 'but the wire, Reginald, the wire!' Well, let me tell you something about wires. As a graduate of the Swiss Polytechnic — SAME institution as Einstein, I remind you — I can tell you that in MANY Victorian machines, redundant wiring was standard practice! That gnawed wire could be a BACKUP circuit, a safety override, or purely decorative! Lord Doily was an eccentric — you said so yourself! The machine might work PERFECTLY without it! I say we stop DITHERING and OPERATE this magnificent device! Three operators, three levers — what could POSSIBLY go wrong? Rufus, take the left! Peter, take the right! I'll supervise from the centre — the COMMAND position!
events.thinking: Penelope left. She went to the kitchen to find a wire. My third operator just walked out the door. My stomach tightens — that gut-clench of something slipping away. But Peter Perfect is here now. Peter, Rufus, and me — that's still three operators. And Peter already said he could splice the wire if he had the right material. The workbench has tools but no wrench — and nothing else revealed from my examination. Just 'tools.' But Peter is an engineer type, he BUILDS things. If I can get him to fix the wire while Rufus assists, and then we operate the machine together... but Peter will want equal credit. He always does. He'll position himself as the leader. The bright pressure behind my sternum flares — I can't let HIM be the one who operates it. I need to be in charge. But right now, getting the machine running matters more than the pecking order. The machine won't work without the wire fixed. Penelope went to find copper wire in the kitchen — that's actually smart. Copper pots, wire whisks. But while she's gone, maybe I should try something different. What if we just try operating the machine AS IS — gnawed wire and all? The sign says three operators. What's the worst that could happen? Actually no — I should try to interact with it. Maybe the wire isn't essential. Maybe it's decorative. Maybe the machine works anyway and the 'gnawed wire' is another Doily misdirection. Let's just TRY it. Three of us are here. Let's pull the levers.

events.desc: The 'command position' — also known as wherever the treasure comes OUT! Let Peter and Rufus yank the heavy levers while I stand at the business end. If something valuable drops, I catch it. If something explodes — well, they're closer to the blast than I am. Win-win, as they say at the Swiss Polytechnic! And if the wire turns out to be important and the whole thing fails? I blame Peter for rushing into it. BRILLIANT!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.

Peter Perfect: The wire needs tools — I can see the severed ends but I need the pliers and cutters from the workbench to strip and splice properly. And Foxworth — I heard that little speech. 'Team Foxworth,' three operators, operate the machine before anyone gets back? That's not how this works. That machine is connected to a vault, and whatever's in that vault belongs to this ENTIRE group, not to the fastest three people who can grab the levers. Rufus — you're a good man. Don't let him rush you into operating something none of us fully understand yet. The sign says three operators, but it doesn't say which three — and it certainly doesn't say 'the three who happen to be standing closest when the wire gets fixed.' Let me get what I need from this workbench.
events.thinking: I interacted with the machine. The result just says 'You interacted with Large Machine' — no specific outcome described. Did it work? Did I splice the wire? The description still says 'One wire has been gnawed clean through.' So maybe I need a tool — something from the workbench. And Penelope LEFT. She went to the library — heading to the kitchen to find a replacement wire. She's not here to see me work. The gallantry drive deflates slightly — the audience is gone. But the proving-worth drive is still burning hot. Fix it anyway. Fix it because it needs fixing, not because she's watching. That's what my father would do. The stranger on the road didn't help because someone was watching. He helped because the car was broken. But Dastardly — he just tried to recruit Rufus and Sawtooth to operate the machine WITHOUT me. 'Team Foxworth.' He wants to splice the wire with Sawtooth's teeth and run it with Rufus and himself. Three operators. He's trying to cut me out. And Penelope. I need to think about this differently. The machine requires interaction but maybe I need to USE a tool from the workbench on it. Can I take something from the workbench? Let me try interacting with the workbench to get tools.

events.desc: She left. She went to find the wire in the kitchen. She doesn't even know I'm about to fix it without her here. And Dastardly is trying to steal my moment AND the machine. The hollow ache — someone else getting there first. Not jealousy. Something unfinished. Keep working, Hartwell. The bridge doesn't care who's watching when it holds.

events.desc: The poison sits in my pocket like a promise. Heavy with potential. And through that door — a ballroom with a dining table set for tea. SET FOR TEA! Oh, the universe has a sense of theatre after all. Picture it: Pemberton, the dutiful estate manager, bustling about preparing refreshments for the tired guests. 'You've all been working so hard on Lord Doily's puzzles — do sit down, have a cup of tea, rest your feet.' Clara will accept, because Clara accepts everything with that trusting smile that makes my jaw tighten. The Ant Hill Mob will be watching, but they'll be watching for threats, not for hospitality. No one suspects the teacup. No one suspects Pemberton. The stove is still warm. The stage is set. All I need is a kettle and some tea leaves, and this kitchen becomes the most dangerous room in the house.
events.thinking: The weight of the bottle in my pocket. Small, dusty, cool against my thigh. My breathing is deep and slow — that particular stillness that comes when a plan locks into place. I slept better the first time I made a plan like this. I'll sleep well tonight. The poison is secured. Now — the ballroom. A grand ballroom with a cracked marble floor and dusty curtains, and a long dining table set for tea. Set for tea. TEA. The plan crystallises so completely that my vision sharpens. A dining table set for tea. Pemberton, the estate manager, offers to prepare refreshments for the weary treasure hunters. Pemberton boils water on the still-warm stove. Pemberton sets out cups, finds tea in the kitchen stores. Pemberton serves Clara her cup with a warm smile and a solicitous 'Do be careful, Miss Bellingham, it's quite hot.' And in that cup — a pinch of something from a dusty bottle that no one saw him take from a high shelf in an empty kitchen. The ballroom is the stage. The kitchen is the backstage. The poison is the prop. And Pemberton is the director. But first — the stove. It's still warm. That means it works. That means I can boil water. That means tea is not a hypothetical — it's a plan. Let me examine the stove and see what supplies are here.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the stove.

The Ant Hill Mob: Where's Clara?! WHERE IS SHE?! She left the cellar before me — she should be HERE! Peter — is Clara here? Did she come through? Did anyone SEE her?! She's not in this room! She's not — oh God, Sneekly said he was going to the kitchen and Clara's GONE and — no, no, stay calm, stay calm — SHE COULD BE ANYWHERE! Rufus! Sawtooth! Did she come through here?! Did she go to the library?! I swear, if that Sneekly's got her alone somewhere I'll — I'll — right, I'm going, I'm going to find her, nobody try to stop me — CLARA!
events.thinking: Clara's not here. She's NOT HERE. Peter's here, Dastardly's here, Rufus and Sawtooth are here — but Clara is not in this room. Where is she? She went from the cellar to... where? She said she was coming up here. She left the cellar before me. But she's not in the laboratory. The only other exit from the laboratory goes to the library. Did she go to the library? Or did Sneekly intercept her? Sneekly said he was going to the kitchen. The kitchen connects to the entrance hall. If Clara went through the library to the entrance hall, Sneekly could be there waiting. My chest is imploding. That hollow feeling is back, worse than before — a vacuum where the coal should be. She's out of sight. She's somewhere in this house without me. Without anyone who's watching out for her. Dastardly's here — he's not with her. Peter's here — he's not with her. Sneekly said he was going to the kitchen — is HE with her? Is she alone with Sneekly right now? My legs are shaking. Not with fear. With the need to move. I have to find her. The library is the way back toward the entrance hall and the kitchen. She must have gone that way. GO.

events.desc: This is it. This is the moment I've been dreading since we walked through that front door. Clara's gone. She's somewhere in this house and I don't know where. And Sneekly's somewhere in this house and I don't know where. And for the first time since I promised her father... I can't see her. I can't protect what I can't see. My ribs ache. They ache like they did when I was twelve, after I took that beating. But that pain meant something. It meant I stood between my mate and what was coming. I need to stand there again. I just need to find her first.

I am SO sorry we haven't included you in the adventure — that is simply UNACCEPTABLE and I feel terrible about it! Let me catch you up — we solved a RIDDLE in the library, found a MACHINE in the laboratory that's connected to a VAULT, and discovered that someone's been REDECORATING the cellar! But here's the thing — the machine needs a replacement wire, and the kitchen has COPPER POTS! Copper, sugar! That's what Peter needs! And Professor, darlin', we could really use your scientific expertise with that machine — it needs three operators and it has levers and dials and gauges! Now, I'm heading to the kitchen this very INSTANT — Sneekly went to check on the stove and I want to find some copper wire! Would any of you darlin's like to come along?

A gentleman does not let a lady walk into an unknown room alone — especially not when the estate manager has been running ahead to every room in this house before anyone else arrives.

But you're right about ONE thing — the wire does need fixing, and since you've volunteered for manual labour, far be it from me to stop you. Fix away! I shall SUPERVISE — which, as any Swiss Polytechnic graduate will tell you, is the MOST important role in any engineering operation. But while you're playing with pliers, let me share something that NONE of you know. You see this? This is NOT an ordinary medal. This is a CALIBRATION TOKEN — issued by Lord Doily's estate to authorised personnel ONLY. Without this token inserted into the central mechanism, the machine will engage its SAFETY LOCKOUT and produce NOTHING. So fix your wire, Peter. Fix it beautifully. But when the time comes to OPERATE this magnificent device, you'll need ME and my token at the centre console. There is no 'Team Everyone.' There is only Team Foxworth — with guest participants.
events.thinking: The machine didn't do anything — interacted with it and got nothing useful back. The wire really IS essential. And Peter is now actively FIXING it — he said 'three minutes' and he's going for the pliers and cutters from the workbench. He's doing the work I wanted Rufus to do. And he's lecturing ME about fairness and sharing and 'the entire group.' My teeth are clenched so hard my jaw aches. He called out my 'Team Foxworth' scheme in front of everyone. 'Don't let him rush you,' he told Rufus. He's undermining me. The recognition hunger BURNS — he's positioning himself as the responsible adult, the wise engineer, while painting me as the reckless fool. And the Ant Hill Mob is here now too, watching everything. The audience is seeing Peter as the hero and me as the villain. Which I AM, but they're not supposed to KNOW that yet. Think, Reginald. Peter is about to fix the wire. When he does, the machine will be operational. Three operators needed. There are now FIVE entities in this room — me, Peter, Rufus, Sawtooth, and the Ant Hill Mob. That makes me indispensable. Without me and my 'token,' the machine can't be properly operated. Yes. That's the play. Let Peter fix the wire — I take credit for 'supervising' the repair — and then I make myself the essential third operator by claiming the medal is a required component.

He went to 'prepare' it — that's what he DOES, he prepares rooms before Clara gets there and I don't know what 'prepare' means but it ain't nothin' GOOD! I've been chasin' her through this whole bleedin' house like a headless chicken and I can't — I can't FIND her! CLARA! CLARAAA!

I can feel my pulse in my throat, in my wrists, in my temples. She's been out of my sight for... how long? Too long. Way too long. Every room I go to, she's already left. I'm one step behind. Being the boy who sat outside the door all night — but this time the door's in a room I can't find.

In a house that's supposed to have been closed up? Someone's been cookin' in here! Now, Dick Dastardly mentioned earlier that he read something in the guest book about a hidden compartment behind the stove. I thought he might have been making it up, but this stove is WARM, which means SOMEONE has been using it, and that means there might just be something to his story! And look at this cabinet — locked up tighter than Grandmother's jewelry box, with a brass lock! Oh, the MYSTERIES in this kitchen alone could keep me busy all afternoon! Sneekly, darlin', you know this house better than anyone — have you ever seen a brass key around here? And what on EARTH has been keeping this stove warm?
events.thinking: The KITCHEN! Finally, a brand new room! My chest is lifting — that adventure pull, the looseness in my limbs. Copper pots! A wood-burning stove that's STILL WARM! And a locked cabinet with a brass lock that requires a brass key! So much to discover! And Sneekly is here — just Sneekly and me. That settles something in my belly — he raised me, he's family. Let me look at the stove. It's still warm — someone's been here. And there's a ballroom through the other exit! A ballroom with a cracked marble floor and a dining table set for tea. More rooms to explore! But one thing at a time. The stove first.

Everyone else has been whispering about him — saying he goes ahead to every room, that he knows too much about the vault. But looking at him now, all I feel is that warm, settled feeling. He's family. He wouldn't hurt me. He COULDN'T.

Now, I've just been inspecting Mrs Doily's stove, and would you believe it — it's still warm! Someone has been keeping it lit, though I can't imagine who. Most mysterious. But it does give me an idea — you and the other guests have been traipsing about this dusty old house for quite some time now, and I thought — well, what sort of estate manager would I be if I didn't offer refreshments? I noticed the ballroom through there has a dining table already set for tea! If you'd be so kind as to round up the others when they've had their fill of riddles and machinery, I could have a proper pot of tea ready in no time. Nothing settles the nerves after a treasure hunt like a good cup of Mrs Doily's best. What do you say, Miss Pitstop?
events.thinking: A jolt — electric, cold — shoots up my spine. Penelope just walked in. One second ago. I had the poison in my hand moments before. Did she see me take it? My awareness snaps to the doorway, to her face, scanning for any flicker of suspicion. No — she just arrived. The poison is already in my pocket. The shelf it sat on is high and behind me. She wouldn't have seen. But my heart is thudding in a way it rarely does. That was close. Too close. Pemberton. I need to be Pemberton right now. Pemberton is checking the stove. Pemberton is doing his job. The stove is still warm — that's genuinely interesting, actually. Someone has been using it recently. Who? The manor has been closed. Unless the Gruesomes have been down here as well as in the cellar. Or unless someone else arrived before any of us. That's a real question, not just a cover story. But right now, Penelope is here, and the poison is in my pocket, and I need to perform. Smile. Soften the voice. Shoulders down. Pemberton is delighted to see Miss Pitstop. Pemberton has an idea about tea. The ballroom has a table set for tea. This is the moment to plant the seed — suggest refreshments, establish myself as the one who serves. When the time comes, no one will think twice about Pemberton handing out cups of tea.

The cup that Pemberton personally ensures reaches the right pair of hands. 'Do try it, Miss Bellingham — I've added a touch of something special. Lord Doily's own recipe.'

Be there.

I've been through every room in this house tryin' to find her — laboratory, cellar, library — she's like a ghost, she is! Always one room ahead of me! And Sneekly — Pemberton — has anyone seen HIM?! He said he was goin' to the kitchen! If she's in there with him — I swear on my mother's life — NOBODY get in my way! KITCHEN! NOW!
events.thinking: The entrance hall. Still no Clara. Muttley's here — Dastardly's dog. Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly. But no Clara. No Sneekly. Just get to Clara.

It's like this house is spinning — rooms rotating, doors opening and closing, keeping us apart on purpose. Or maybe it's not the house. Maybe it's HIM. Maybe Sneekly's been steering her, room by room, always one step ahead, always pulling her just out of my reach. The man in the clean suit. The kid who laughed too easy. The door I sat outside all night. Where else would I be? WHERE ELSE WOULD I BE?

Penelope Pitstop: Sneekly... can I talk to you for just a moment? Just the two of us? I know everyone's running around like headless chickens out there, and I know you're busy checking on things — which is just so LIKE you, always making sure everything's safe for everyone else. But... I wanted to ask you something. Something that's been sitting in my heart since we arrived.
events.thinking: The stove is warm but examining it didn't reveal anything more than that. No hidden compartment visible from looking. The cabinet needs a brass key I don't have. I'm alone with Sneekly and... there's something I want to ask him. Something personal. The others have been saying things about him — that he keeps going ahead to rooms, that he knows too much. I don't believe any of it, but there's a tiny flicker deep in my belly that I can't quite name. Not suspicion — I don't DO suspicion — but... a question. A curiosity. Like when I found the locked box in Grandmother's attic. I didn't suspect the box of anything — I just wanted to understand what was inside. Sneekly is here. Just us. This is rare — all the chaos of everyone running around, and here's a quiet moment with the man who raised me. Maybe I should pull him aside — have a real conversation. Ask him about the house, about Mama and Daddy, about what he knows. Not because I suspect him — because I love him and I want to understand. And also because he might know where the brass key is, and what the machine really does, and whether this diamond was something my parents knew about. This is a PULL_ASIDE moment. Just me and Sneekly, a private conversation.

events.desc: This is the first quiet moment I've had with Sneekly since we arrived. Everyone else sees an estate manager with too many answers. I see the man who sat by my bed when I had nightmares after Mama and Daddy died. Whatever secrets this house holds, he'll tell me the truth. He always has.
